item.title: $1bn refinery deal powers Bangladesh’s push for next growth engine
item.description:
Bangladesh has secured $1 billion in financing from the Islamic Development Bank to expand Eastern Refinery as the government seeks to strengthen energy security and build a new manufacturing-driven growth model beyond the garment industry.
The agreement, signed on Thursday in the presence of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and IsDB Group President Dr Muhammad Al Jasser, will finance the modernization and expansion of the state-owned refinery and increase its annual crude oil processing capacity by 3 million tons.
Tarique described the deal as more than a financial transaction, calling it a “statement of confidence” in Bangladesh and linking energy security directly to the government’s ambition to turn the country into a regional manufacturing hub.
“Garments built our first growth story. Now we want electronics, pharmaceuticals, light engineering, and green industry to build the next one,” he said. “We want factories that create jobs and dignity.”
The prime minister said the government aims to build a trillion-dollar economy by 2034 and double the size of the economy this decade through exports, investment and financial discipline.
“This is not a slogan. It is a plan,” he said.
Tarique said the refinery expansion would strengthen Bangladesh’s energy security, economic resilience and long-term growth capacity at a time when geopolitical conflicts, supply-chain disruptions and energy insecurity are putting increasing pressure on developing economies.
Economic Relations Division Additional Secretary Dr Md Mizanur Rahman and IsDB Director General for Country Programmes Anasse Aissami signed the agreement on behalf of Bangladesh and the bank respectively at the Bangladesh Secretariat.
The prime minister said Bangladesh now wants a broader relationship with IsDB, seeking more innovative, low-cost and results-oriented financing aligned with the country’s development priorities.
He said Bangladesh was particularly interested in benefiting from IsDB’s Islamic Concessional Fund, with the ERD and the bank’s Dhaka hub already working to identify potential projects.
Tarique also urged IsDB to act as a bridge among member countries with different strengths in energy, infrastructure and other sectors.
“Let the members build with each other, not just alongside each other,” he said.

item.title: SRB to replace RAB under new law
item.description:
The government has moved to abolish the Rapid Action Battalion and replace it with a new specialized force under the police, introducing legislation in the National Parliament on Thursday that would fundamentally restructure one of Bangladesh’s key law enforcement agencies.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed introduced the Special Response Battalion (SRB) Act, 2026 bill, which proposes transferring RAB’s personnel, assets and responsibilities to a newly created Special Response Battalion.
The bill was subsequently sent to the parliamentary standing committee for scrutiny.
Under the proposed law, the SRB will operate as a specialised unit of the police, tasked with combating terrorism and organized crime, recovering illegal firearms and drugs, tackling cybercrime and preventing violence against women and children.
Its headquarters will be in Dhaka, with a director general exercising administrative and operational authority.
SRB personnel would have powers to search, seize and arrest, but the bill stipulates that those powers must be exercised in accordance with existing laws.
The proposed legislation also introduces disciplinary provisions, including dismissal, demotion and fines for misconduct.
Significantly, the bill provides for a grievance redressal committee aimed at strengthening human rights protection and accountability within the new force.
Once the legislation comes into effect, RAB’s manpower, resources and operational responsibilities will be transferred to the SRB, effectively bringing an end to the existing force.
The government says the restructuring is necessary to create a modern and accountable specialized law enforcement unit capable of responding to changing patterns of crime and emerging national security challenges.

36 Bangladeshis among 96 detained at Bosnia border
item.description:
Ninety-six people, including 36 Bangladeshis, have been detained by border police in Bosnia and Herzegovina for allegedly attempting to illegally cross the country’s border.
The Gradiska Border Police, with assistance from the Ministry of Interior of Republika Srpska, foiled two attempts to illegally cross the border on Wednesday, according to reports published Thursday by Sarajevo Times and First Balkan Media.
According to the Bosnia and Herzegovina Border Police, the first attempt involved 63 people and was stopped in Bistrica on Wednesday afternoon. The group included 40 Pakistani nationals and 23 Bangladeshis.
Acting on instructions from the prosecutor on duty at the Prosecutor’s Office of Bosnia and Herzegovina, authorities seized two boats at the scene and identified two people suspected of involvement in human trafficking.
Later that night, another attempt involving 33 people was foiled in Bistrica. The group included 13 Bangladeshis, 18 Afghans and two Pakistanis.
Authorities said the Banja Luka Field Centre of the Service for Foreigners’ Affairs had been informed of the incidents and that legal proceedings were underway.

item.description:

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir handed over the contribution to Nepal Ambassador to Bangladesh Ghanshyam Bhandari at State Guest House Padma on Wednesday.
Kobir conveyed a letter from Prime Minister Tarique Rahman addressed to Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah.
Earlier, on September 1, 2026, Kobir signed the condolence book opened at the Embassy of Nepal in Dhaka.
The Bangladesh National Parliament also adopted a condolence motion on August 27, 2026, following the tragedy in Nepal.

Dhaka airport import cargo without scanner for 10 months
item.description:
The import cargo facility at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport has been without a scanner for the past 10 months, forcing Customs officials to rely on bills of entry and physical inspections to assess imported goods.
The absence of the scanner has raised concerns over the ability to detect illicit goods being brought into the country under the cover of legitimate consignments.
The issue came into focus after customs authorities recently seized 16kg of gold concealed inside fruit cartons from the airport’s import cargo facility.
The seizure was made based on prior intelligence, with customs officials later searching the consignment and recovering the gold.
Dhaka Customs House Commissioner Mashiur Rahman disclosed the information at a press conference held Thursday afternoon following the seizure of 20kg of gold at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.
He said the scanner at the import cargo facility was damaged in a fire on October 18 last year and has not been replaced since.
“The process of purchasing a scanner is underway,” he said.
According to sources, customs officials seized 16kg of gold specially concealed inside fruit cartons from the import cargo facility on July 19.
Later, information emerged that another 10 consignments from the same company had arrived at the airport.
Those concerned said there was no way to guarantee that gold or other illicit goods had not been smuggled through those consignments.
They said Customs officials currently examine bills of entry and physically inspect imported goods. However, given the volume of cargo handled at the facility, it is not always possible to thoroughly inspect every item in large consignments.
As a result, large quantities of goods could potentially leave the facility without adequate examination, they said.
“This is a major threat for us,” they added.
Khairul Kabir Bhuiyan Mithu, vice-president of the C&F Agents Association, said having a scanner at the import cargo facility was essential.
“We have been hearing for several months that a scanner is coming. But it has not arrived yet,” he said.
Meanwhile, Customs Additional Commissioner Kamrul Islam said it was incorrect to suggest that goods were leaving the facility without inspection because there was no scanner.
“Our officials physically check every consignment,” he said.
However, having a scanner would make the inspection process easier, he added.
Scanner damaged in airport fire
A fire broke out at the Cargo Village Complex of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at noon on October 18 last year.
Thirty-seven units from 13 fire stations worked for nearly six and a half hours to bring the blaze under control.
Goods worth hundreds of crores of taka were destroyed in the fire.
The scanner at the import cargo facility was also damaged in the incident and has remained out of operation since then.

item.title: CAB slams decision to scrap interim govt's essential drugs list
item.description: The Consumers Association of Bangladesh (CAB) has demanded immediate government action to resolve the ongoing electricity and gas crisis, and to reinstate the recently scrapped list of essential medicines, warning that consumer suffering has reached an extreme level. The demands came at a discussion meeting titled "Protest against inadequate electricity and gas supply and the decision to scrap the essential medicine list," organized by CAB at its Segunbagicha office in the capital on Thursday. Addressing the meeting, CAB President AHM Shafiquzzaman said around 400 mills have already shut down amid the fuel crisis, raising the risk of higher production costs and unemployment. He said gas and oil prices, transport extortion and system loss were fuelling public suffering, and called for a reduction in import dependence to ensure domestic industry and fuel availability and move towards self-reliance. He also urged the government to inform the public about the rationale behind scrapping the essential drugs list and take effective steps to control medicine prices, cautioning the authorities to adopt a pro-people policy ensuring safe food and medicine supplies. On August 3, 2026, a cabinet decision scrapped the Essential Medicines List 2026 and the Drug Price Determination Method 2026, both implemented by the interim government at the start of the year. Most notably, the interim government's framework expanded price-controlled generic drugs from 117 to 295. The latest decision of the BNP government reverts to a 1994 law, and the prices for almost 180 additional medicines that were briefly facing state regulation will instead be determined directly by private pharmaceutical companies under Directorate General of Drug Administration (DGDA) oversight. Speakers at today's CAB event clearly stated that it is a broken model. CAB Central Secretary General Humayun Kabir Bhuiyan said consumer suffering had peaked due to the gas-electricity crisis and the scrapping of the interim government's essential medicines list. "We are not against the government; rather, we are playing an advocacy role, standing beside the government in the public interest," he said, urging authorities to identify those responsible and take swift, effective measures to ease consumer hardship. CAB Treasurer Md Shawkat Ali Khan said adulteration has "taken the shape of an epidemic," adding that various problems already existed around medicines even before the essential drug list was abruptly scrapped, worsening the crisis further. He called for restoring the essential medicine list to ensure logical pricing and availability, along with strict measures against adulterated medicine and food to safeguard public health. Bangladesh Sadharan Nagorik Samaj convener Mohiuddin Ahmed said the energy crisis requires specific solutions, calling for effective measures to boost domestic gas extraction and ensure fuel supply, and stressed the need for long-term energy planning to reduce import dependence. CAB advisor Khalilur Rahman, Organizing Secretary Abul Kalam Azad, Publicity Secretary Anwar Hossain Chowdhury, and Executive Committee Member Anwar Hossain were also present at the discussion. The event was moderated by CAB Executive Director Ahmed Ekramullah.

item.title: ChatGPT hit by widespread outage as reports surge past 43,000
item.description:
ChatGPT suffered a widespread disruption on Thursday, with tens of thousands of users reporting problems accessing or using the AI platform as OpenAI investigated issues affecting ChatGPT and Codex.
Reports on outage-tracking service Downdetector rose rapidly, from more than 5,000 shortly before 9pm Bangladesh time to over 22,000 within minutes and then past 43,000, indicating a sharp escalation in the disruption.
OpenAI initially showed no problems on its official status page before acknowledging that it was investigating issues affecting ChatGPT and Codex.
The company had not immediately disclosed the cause.
The disruption came after several service problems in recent days.
Earlier Thursday, OpenAI reported high error rates affecting ChatGPT Work Mode.
That incident began at 6:04am Bangladesh time and was resolved six minutes later.
On Wednesday, the company resolved errors preventing some users from creating new accounts, while ChatGPT Work also experienced elevated errors and latency earlier in the week.
OpenAI notes that its availability figures are aggregated across subscription tiers, models and error types, meaning individual users may encounter problems even when its overall status appears normal.
The scale of Thursday’s user reports made the latest disruption potentially one of the more significant ChatGPT service interruptions in recent days, although the full extent and cause remained unclear.

item.title: TIB: Hopes for independent NHRC remain unfulfilled
item.description:
Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) has said that proposed laws on the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) and enforced disappearances still fail to ensure independent, impartial and conflict-free investigations into serious human rights violations.
The anti-graft watchdog said several positive amendments were proposed by the parliamentary standing committee during its review of the National Human Rights Commission Bill, 2026 and the Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Bill, 2026.
However, it said fundamental weaknesses remain, particularly regarding the NHRC’s ability to independently investigate allegations against law enforcement agencies on its own initiative.
Against the backdrop of Bangladesh’s experience of prolonged and serious human rights violations, TIB called for meaningful parliamentary discussion on every important provision of the two bills before their passage, with participation from both government and opposition lawmakers.
TIB welcomed several recommendations made by the parliamentary committee on the NHRC bill, including mandatory representation of indigenous or disadvantaged communities, disqualification of loan defaulters from becoming commissioners, and removal of the requirement for prior approval to visit detention centres other than military detention centres.
However, TIB Executive Director Dr Iftekharuzzaman said the proposed law still does not provide sufficient safeguards for an independent commission.
“The absence of a clear provision that the Commission shall not fall under any ministry or division of the government; the scope for a serving government employee to become a commissioner while on deputation, lien or unpaid leave; the risk of unchecked executive influence through the composition of the selection committee; the deputation of up to 30% of the Commission’s total staff from government service; and the failure to guarantee full financial independence together mean that hopes for a genuinely independent Human Rights Commission remain unfulfilled,” he said.
He said the proposed structure could result in a commission being established without ensuring its independence.
“In other words, a commission is being formed, but the hope that it will be independent remains an illusion,” he said.
Dr Iftekharuzzaman also questioned provisions under which the commission would have to seek reports from the relevant force or institution instead of conducting its own investigation into serious human rights violations by disciplinary forces.
He said the proposed arrangement effectively leaves investigative authority in the hands of institutions accused of violations.
TIB also expressed concern that military detention centres have been excluded from the places that the National Preventive Mechanism unit may inspect regularly and without prior notice.
The organisation said the proposed bill has also narrowed several important functions of the commission, including providing legal assistance to aggrieved persons, conducting human rights training, examining the consistency of laws with international human rights instruments, and undertaking other activities necessary to promote and protect human rights.
Regarding the Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Bill, TIB said the parliamentary committee had not recommended any fundamental change to the core investigative framework.
The organisation described the proposed amendments as largely “cosmetic” in terms of ensuring independent investigations, accountability and victims’ rights.
Dr Iftekharuzzaman said Section 19 of the NHRC bill retains the arrangement under which the commission would seek a report from the concerned force or institution in cases involving serious human rights violations by disciplinary forces.
“By narrowing the Commission’s power of inquiry and investigation and making it dependent on reports, this provision makes it weaker than even the 2009 law and inconsistent with the Paris Principles,” he said.
He said the enforced disappearance bill has a similar weakness.
Although Section 14(3) bars an accused force from investigating its own members, the provision allows responsibility to be assigned to another disciplinary force or an inter-force investigation team.
TIB questioned whether such an arrangement could ensure genuine independence when members of various disciplinary, police, intelligence and security agencies have been accused of involvement in past enforced disappearance cases.
“Is the investigating institution genuinely independent from that same justice-obstructing institutional circle, or is it being asked to investigate itself?” Dr Iftekharuzzaman asked.
He warned that a weak or biased investigation could obstruct justice and deprive victims and their families of recognition, compensation and rights relating to the use and inheritance of property.
TIB also called for a more comprehensive definition of enforced disappearance in line with the International Convention for the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance (ICPPED).
Dr Iftekharuzzaman said the definition should explicitly cover possible involvement by public representatives, MPs, ministers, advisers and other influential state actors, alongside government employees and members of disciplinary forces.
He also raised concerns over Section 15, saying it was unclear how an accused senior official could be shielded from proceedings based on an interim report prepared by a subordinate investigator without the process being vulnerable to influence.
He said this could create a risk of impunity for accused officials.
TIB further pointed out that Section 16 does not retain safeguards included in the 2025 ordinance requiring searches to continue until a disappeared person is found or their fate is established and requiring families to be regularly informed of progress.
The organisation also said penalties for some offences have been reduced compared with the 2025 ordinance.
While the minimum sentence for enforced disappearance remains three years, the bill provides for a maximum of five years’ rigorous imprisonment for false or harassing accusations.
Dr Iftekharuzzaman warned that such a provision could discourage families from filing complaints if the investigation process itself is vulnerable to conflicts of interest and institutional influence.
“When the investigation mechanism itself carries the risk of conflict of interest and institutional influence, there is a real concern that, for want of adequate evidence, the failure to prove a genuine allegation could instead be blamed on the complainant’s family,” he said.
“Such a provision risks creating a serious culture of fear among victims when it comes to lodging complaints and seeking justice.”
TIB said it had shared its observations on the NHRC law from the drafting stage and, following Cabinet approval, submitted 25 recommendations on the NHRC bill and 17 recommendations on the Enforced Disappearance Prevention Bill.
Dr Iftekharuzzaman said the parliamentary review provided an opportunity to address the fundamental weaknesses in the two bills, but several core concerns raised by stakeholders remain unresolved.
“We expect that, instead of being passed hastily by voice vote, the bills will be amended following meaningful discussion in Parliament on every important provision and proposed amendment, with all members rising above partisan loyalty and guided by their moral and humane values,” he said.
He warned that if the 13th Parliament passes the bills without the necessary amendments to bring them in line with the Paris Principles, ICPPED and other international standards, it would fail to meet public expectations for human rights protection.
The call comes amid broader concerns from rights groups that the proposed framework leaves investigations into enforced disappearance with the police rather than establishing an independent investigative mechanism.

State Minister Shama urges investment in cosmetics industry
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam has called for greater local and foreign investment in Bangladesh’s cosmetics, skincare and personal care industry, saying the sector has the potential to become a major manufacturing and export hub.
She made the remarks while inaugurating Cosmética Dhaka 2026 at the International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB) in Dhaka on Thursday.
Speaking as the chief guest, Shama Obaed said Bangladesh could leverage the production capacity, compliance infrastructure, skilled workforce and global buyer networks developed through its readymade garment industry to build a competitive cosmetics sector.
“By leveraging the production capacity, compliance infrastructure, skilled workforce and global buyer relationships that we have developed in the readymade garment industry, it is possible to establish contract manufacturing, formulation, specialized packaging, quality laboratories and certification facilities in the cosmetics sector as well,” she said.
She also highlighted the potential of Bangladesh’s agricultural and natural resources.
“If we can build a strong supply chain of certified botanical and herbal ingredients by utilizing Bangladesh’s agriculture and natural resources, this sector will not only meet domestic demand but also open new export opportunities for Bangladesh in the global market,” she said.
The state minister said the government wanted to take the industry beyond “Made in Bangladesh” towards “Formulated, Developed and Branded in Bangladesh”.
She called for investment facilitation, internationally recognized testing and certification, intellectual property protection, sustainable packaging and support for small and medium-sized entrepreneurs.
“If we can establish an integrated industrial base by ensuring environmentally friendly production, safe raw materials and international standards, the cosmetics and personal care sector could emerge as a new and powerful area for foreign currency earnings, employment generation and economic diplomacy in Bangladesh,” she added.
Cosmética Dhaka 2026 features brands, manufacturers, suppliers, retailers and health experts from 16 countries, including South Korea, Thailand, the United States, France, Singapore, China, Japan and India.
The three-day exhibition has more than 100 stalls, along with live demonstrations, beauty consultations, expert discussions and networking opportunities.
BIAA President Baharul Monsur said the cosmetics and personal care industry had been growing every year and called for more investment through the exhibition.
Frank Kenton, senior perfumer at Senses International Ltd, said Bangladesh was one of the promising markets in South Asia, but products must remain affordable for consumers.
SM Faisal Munim, CEO of Squad Mind Global Ltd, said the organizers expected the exhibition to attract more local and foreign investment and establish itself as a business-matching platform.
The exhibition will remain open to visitors from 10am to 7pm every day.

item.title: Thirty injured as picnic bus collides head-on with passenger bus in Natore
item.description:
At least 30 teachers, students and guardians of Shaheen School’s Sirajganj branch were injured when a bus carrying them collided head-on with a passenger bus in Baraigram upazila of Natore on Thursday.
The accident occurred around 10am in the Manikpur area of the Bonpara-Hatikumrul highway as the school group was travelling to Safina Park in Rajshahi for an annual picnic.
The collision left the front sections of both buses badly damaged. Traffic on the highway remained halted for about an hour before the vehicles were removed and movement resumed, reports Bangla Tribune.
According to eyewitness Hossain Ali, the school bus was heading towards Rajshahi when it collided head-on with a Dhaka-bound passenger bus in Manikpur. No one was killed, but at least 30 people travelling on the picnic bus were injured.
The injured include Rezaul Karim, 39; Zainal Abedin, 26; Sinha Islam, 7; Sonali Khatun, 25; Barsha Khatun, 20; Taslim Ahmed, 33; Hazrat Ali, 50; Dighi Khatun, 12; Rabbi Hasan, 24; Ashraful Islam, 42; Beauty Begum, 26; Hawa Begum, 30; Monirul Islam, 33; Habiba Khatun, 12; another Rezaul Karim, 45; Kabya Hossain, 12; and Mostafizur Rahman, 46.
Fire Service personnel from Bonpara, highway police and local residents rescued the injured and took them to Baraigram Upazila Health Complex and Amina Hospital in Bonpara for treatment.
Five teachers of Shaheen School alleged that the passenger bus was travelling recklessly at high speed and suddenly rammed into their bus. Some passengers fell from their seats while others were thrown against the windows, causing panic inside the bus.
The driver of the passenger bus fled the scene following the crash, they said.
The school’s picnic programme has been cancelled following the accident. The injured are being taken back to Sirajganj after receiving treatment.
SI Alamgir Hossain of Bonpara Highway Police Station said the two buses involved in the accident had been seized.

item.title: Ziaur Rahman Medical College interns call off strike
item.description:
Intern doctors at Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Medical College (SHZMC) Hospital in Bogra called off their two-day strike on Thursday after authorities assured them of increased security and action against those accused of attacking doctors.
The interns began the strike at midnight on Tuesday after several colleagues were injured when relatives of a patient who died at the hospital allegedly attacked doctors on duty.
They decided to resume work following a nearly three-hour meeting involving political leaders, the district administration and hospital authorities at the hospital auditorium on Thursday.
Intern doctor Ritul Mondal Snigdha confirmed the decision.
SHZMC Hospital Deputy Director Dr Manzur-e-Morshed said the meeting was held in a cordial atmosphere and the interns agreed to return to work after being assured that their demands would be addressed.
Their demands included expelling those involved in the attack who allegedly acted in the name of the Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD), increasing police presence, deploying armed Ansar personnel and appointing the required staff for 18 beds.
The interns resumed their normal duties from Thursday night, the deputy director said.
Meanwhile, five JCD leaders were expelled from the organization over their alleged involvement in the incident.
Abdul Malek, of Rajapur village in Bogra Sadar, died while undergoing treatment in the Medicine Ward on the seventh floor of the hospital at around 10pm on Tuesday.
Following his death, his relatives allegedly attacked doctors on duty with locally made weapons. Several doctors were injured, including intern doctor Mohammad Ali Jinnah, who suffered a broken hand, and Azraf Islam, who sustained bleeding injuries.
At a press briefing on Wednesday, the interns said at least 15 of their colleagues had been injured, six of them seriously.
The attackers also allegedly vandalized medical equipment and government property, causing an estimated Tk2.1 lakh in damage. Three mobile phones and a stethoscope were reportedly taken from the ward.
Police rushed to the hospital and brought the situation under control.
Hospital Ward Master Anwar Hossain filed a case with Bogra Sadar police station, naming seven people and eight to 10 unidentified individuals as accused.
Police arrested six people on Wednesday afternoon and, following a court order, sent them to Bogra jail.
While Thursday’s meeting was underway, Bogra city JCD announced the expulsion of five leaders for disciplinary violations.
They are Ward 18 Convener Nafiul Islam, Senior Joint Convener Monir Hossain, Joint Convener Md Pranto Islam, member Rakibul Hasan Rakib and Ward 19 Assistant Organizational Secretary SM Shihab.
District JCD President Habibur Rashid Sandhan said strict organizational and legal action was being taken against those involved in the attack.
The interns’ strike disrupted services at the hospital for two days, although emergency services remained operational. Patients and their relatives travelling from different areas faced difficulties.
At around 10am on Thursday, the interns also closed the outpatient department ticket counter, causing anger among patients and their relatives. The counter reopened after hospital authorities intervened.
During Thursday’s meeting, District Commissioner Toufikur Rahman, Police Superintendent Mirza Sayem Mahmud, District Council Administrator AKM Ahsanul Tayeb Zakir, Bogra City Corporation Administrator MR Islam Swadhin, former SHZMC principal Professor Dr Moudud Hossain Alamgir Pavel, current principal Professor Dr Wadudul Haque Tarafdar, Deputy Director Dr Manzur-e-Morshed, medical leaders, and social and political leaders were present.
Hospital services returned to normal after the interns called off their strike.

item.title: Myanmar vows ‘safe’ returns ahead of Malaysia repatriations
item.description:
Myanmar pledged on Thursday “safe and dignified” returns for its citizens displaced abroad, after the United Nations and rights groups raised concerns about the upcoming repatriation of 1,500 people from Malaysia.
The Myanmar foreign ministry also repeated its disavowal of the persecuted Rohingya Muslim minority, members of which campaigners fear may be plunged back into danger by the return scheme.
In July, Malaysia said Myanmar had agreed to take back 5,000 members of the Rohingya, a group which has faced a campaign of violent discrimination in Myanmar since 2017.
Both countries say a first wave of nearly 1,500 Myanmar nationals will be repatriated voluntarily in late September, although it is unclear how many Rohingya will be included.
“Myanmar is committed to working closely with Bangladesh and friendly countries to facilitate the voluntary return of verified displaced persons in a safe and dignified manner,” the foreign ministry statement said.
Hundreds of thousands of Rohingya fled Myanmar after a brutal military crackdown starting in 2017, which is the basis of a genocide case at the International Court of Justice.
More than 1.2 million live just over the border in Bangladesh, in the world’s largest refugee settlement, but talk of repatriations has yielded little progress.
Another 126,000 Rohingya live in Malaysia, alongside displaced Myanmar citizens from different ethnic groups.
Myanmar has long denied the Rohingya have a distinct heritage, saying they are descendants of immigrants from Bangladesh -- even refusing to use the term “Rohingya.”
The foreign ministry repeated its assertion on Thursday that the term “falsely claims an ethnic identity which has never existed in Myanmar,” as it condemned recent commemorations in some countries for Rohingya Genocide Remembrance Day.
Malaysia’s communications minister Fahmi Fadzil has said his country will not repatriate Myanmar nationals “if they would either be persecuted or their lives would be threatened.”
But rights monitors fear returning the Rohingya to a country where their identities are erased will permit a new wave of abuses.
A report by UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres published Wednesday found “conditions for their voluntary, safe, dignified and sustainable return do not currently exist.”
Many migrants in Malaysia are also being held in detention centers, raising questions about whether their decisions to return can be freely made.

429 arrested, weapons recovered in DMP raids over 24 hours
item.description:
A total of 429 people were arrested in regular raids conducted by the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) across the capital over the past 24 hours.
During the operations, police also recovered several illegal firearms, 822 yaba pills, 19kg 185g of cannabis and 88 bottles of Eskaf syrup. A total of 64 cases were filed during the period.
Deputy Commissioner of the DMP’s Media and Public Relations Division Md Akter Hossain confirmed the information on Thursday.
Four people were arrested in connection with a gunfight in Gandaria, and a foreign-made pistol and yaba were recovered following the incident.
In a separate operation in Banani, five people were arrested with a foreign-made pistol while allegedly preparing to commit a robbery.
In Mirpur, notorious criminal and shooter Zakir was arrested with firearms and ammunition.
Meanwhile, the DMP’s City Intelligence Analysis Division arrested a suspected drug dealer and recovered 7kg of cannabis.
Of the 429 arrested, 22 were detained by the Ramna Division, 22 by the Lalbagh Division, 39 by the Wari Division, 66 by the Motijheel Division, 62 by the Tejgaon Division, 144 by the Mirpur Division, 35 by the Gulshan Division, 39 by the Uttara Division and two by the Detective Branch.
The arrests were made during operations in various police station areas across the capital, where police also recovered other evidence and narcotics.
Legal proceedings against the arrested individuals are underway, the DMP said.

item.title: Madrasa student death: Father protests teacher’s bail, questions suicide theory
item.description:
The father of an eight-year-old madrasa student found hanging in a teachers’ toilet in Jatrabari on Thursday questioned how his son could have died by suicide as a Dhaka court granted bail to one of three teachers accused in the case.
“An eight-year-old child cannot commit suicide. My son could not even tie a mosquito-net rope. How could he hang himself?” Ziaur Rahman said after the court granted bail to Hafez Mohammad Ullah.
He also questioned how the knot around his son’s neck had been tied, saying even a sensible person could not have made such a knot.
Ziaur Rahman was present at the court to oppose Mohammad Ullah’s bail and expressed frustration over the order, as well as the fact that the other two accused teachers have not been arrested.
“They are moving around openly. The law enforcement agencies are not arresting them,” he said.
Dhaka’s 15th Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge Mizanur Rahman granted Mohammad Ullah bail after hearing arguments from both sides.
SM Abul Kalam (Azad), lawyer for the complainant, confirmed the matter.
The court granted Mohammad Ullah bail on a Tk1,000 bond until the police report is submitted.
Mohammad Ullah was arrested nearly two months after the case was filed and has remained in jail since then.
During the hearing, his lawyer, Abul Kalam Khan, sought bail, saying his client was not involved in the incident and had been implicated in the case as part of a conspiracy.
He said Mohammad Ullah was the sole earning member of his family and that his detention had left his family struggling.
“Any condition may be imposed for his bail,” the lawyer said.
Opposing the bail, Alhaz Borhan Uddin, chief prosecutor in the BDR mutiny case, said CCTV footage from the madrasa showed the child appearing cheerful and energetic on the afternoon of the incident.
He said it was suspicious that the eight-year-old was later found dead in the teachers’ toilet with a gamcha, a traditional thin cotton towel, around his neck.
“The accused killed the child. We oppose his bail,” he said.
Child found dead in teachers’ toilet
On December 20 last year, Mudachchir’s body was recovered from the teachers’ toilet on the fourth floor of Madrasatul Itqan Li Ulumil Quran in Kutubkhali, Jatrabari.
The child was found with a gamcha wrapped around his neck.
The following day, his father filed a murder case against three teachers — Maulana Qari Anisur Rahman, teacher-in-charge Hafez Maulana Zahirul Islam and Hafez Mohammad Ullah.
According to the case statement, Ziaur Rahman suspects that the accused may have attempted to sexually assault his son or that the child may have witnessed an incident involving them.
He alleged that the three accused, along with four or five unidentified people, killed Mudachchir sometime between 4:15pm and 6:30pm on December 20.
He further alleged that the body was hung from the ventilation of the teachers’ toilet with a gamcha to divert the investigation.
The other two accused have yet to be arrested, according to the father.

item.title: Court orders seizure of ex-railway minister’s 18 plots, 2 cars
item.description:
A Dhaka court has ordered the seizure of 18 plots of land in Comilla, along with two Toyota vehicles owned by former railway minister Md Mujibul Haque, in a corruption case. The court also ordered the freezing of six bank accounts held in his name.
Dhaka Metropolitan Senior Special Judge Md Shahjahan Kabir passed the order on Thursday following an application by Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) Assistant Director Papon Kumar Saha.
According to the ACC, Mujibul Haque allegedly abused his power while serving as a public servant, including as railway minister and lawmaker, and, in collusion with others, acquired and possessed Tk7.39 crore in assets beyond his known sources of income through dishonest means.
The ACC filed the case against him under Section 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, and Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947.
During the investigation, scrutiny of records found that attempts were being made to transfer or dispose of movable and immovable assets owned by or linked to the accused, the ACC said in its application.
The commission said transferring or disposing of the assets before the case is resolved could cause significant financial loss, prompting it to seek the court’s order to secure the properties.

item.title: Minister Millat’s vehicle fined after driving on wrong side in Dhaka
item.description:
Traffic police stopped a vehicle carrying Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat in Dhaka on Thursday morning after it was allegedly found driving on the wrong side of the road, filing two cases and imposing Tk 6,000 in fines.
The incident took place after 9am when the Range Rover, bearing registration number Dhaka Metro-Gha-18-2125, was traveling toward the Secretariat after passing in front of Kakrail Mosque, according to sources familiar with the incident.
A Traffic Ramna Division official wishing to be anonymous, said the vehicle had violated its lane and was obstructing normal traffic movement. The official said traffic police stopped the vehicle in front of the Secretariat and informed its driver, Arif Hossain, that driving on the wrong side of the road in such a manner was a violation of traffic rules.
The official said the vehicle was carrying a flag and that the minister was inside when traffic police stopped it. A traffic officer on duty subsequently detained the vehicle, and the cases were filed in the presence of senior officials.
Traffic Sergeant Sifat Mahmud, who was on duty at the time, filed the two cases.
The two cases carry fines of Tk 3,000 each, totaling Tk 6,000. One case was filed for creating an obstruction to traffic movement, while the other was for driving the vehicle unsafely.
Speaking to the media about the incident, Sergeant Sifat said: “I could not believe that a case could be filed against a minister’s vehicle. It is a rare incident.”
He said the traffic control room had also been informed about the incident and that the Special Security Force (SSF) had instructed them to take action.
“The driver of the vehicle also admitted to violating traffic rules,” Sifat said.

item.title: Shapla Chattar case: ICT orders Hasina, 29 others to surrender
item.description:
The International Crimes Tribunal-2 on Thursday ordered 30 people, including ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, to surrender before the tribunal by September 16 in a case over the alleged Shapla Chattar massacre during a Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh rally in 2013.
The three-member ICT-2, headed by Justice Nozrul Islam Chowdhury, passed the order and directed the authorities concerned to publish advertisements in daily newspapers notifying the accused of the order.
The tribunal also set September 30 for the next hearing in the case.
Ten arrested accused, including former minister Hasanul Haque Inu, writer Shahriar Kabir and former minister Dipu Moni, were produced before the tribunal on Thursday.
However, journalist Farzana Rupa was not brought before the tribunal as she was unwell.
The other accused produced before the tribunal were former state minister for home Shamsul Haque Tuku, former food minister Dr Abdur Razzaque, former minister Abdul Latif Siddiqui, former IGP AKM Shahidul Haque, Major General (retd) Ziaul Ahsan, former DIG Abdul Jalil Mondal and former managing director of Ekattor TV Mozammel Haque Babu.
Earlier, on August 16, 11 accused were scheduled to be produced before the tribunal.
On July 27, ICT-2 took cognizance of the formal charges filed by the prosecution against 41 accused.
The case involves two charges, including the killing of 32 people at Shapla Chattar on May 5, 2013, and the killing of 20 people on May 6 in Siddhirganj, Narayanganj, and other parts of the country.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 986 as three die in 24 hours
item.description:
Three children died with measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours until 8:00am on Thursday, raising the country’s combined number of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 986 this year.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all three latest fatalities as suspected measles deaths.
With these, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 887, while confirmed deaths from measles have remained the same at 99.
A total of 964 new suspected measles cases were reported during the 24-hour period, bringing the cumulative number of suspected cases nationwide to 161,148.
Meanwhile, 80 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 19,527.
Since March 15 this year, a total of 141,449 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalised across the country, of whom 136,405 have recovered, according to DGHS data.

item.title: El Nino could be strongest in decades, UN warns
item.description:
El Nino could be the strongest since records began four decades ago, the United Nations’ climate agency warned Thursday, with the UN chief warning the world is in the “danger zone of extreme weather.”
The naturally-occurring weather phenomenon is set to become “very strong” in the months ahead and is near certain to persist through to February, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said.
El Nino warms surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean, bringing worldwide changes in winds, pressure and rainfall patterns.
“If this trajectory continues, it may be stronger than anything since our monitoring began -- so literally off the charts we have used for the past four decades,” WMO chief Celeste Saulo told reporters in Geneva.
El Nino will peak towards the end of this year -- though its knock-on impacts for the climate will continue well into 2027, said the WMO.
Heat in the oceans releases more slowly into the atmosphere, pushing up global temperatures the following year.
The powerful 2023-24 El Nino contributed to 2024 being the warmest year on record, and “we should not be surprised if this record is broken,” Saulo added.
“El Nino is firmly established and will intensify into a very strong event in the coming months, with big impacts on rainfall and temperature patterns and associated risks of floods, drought and extreme heat,” the WMO said.
El Nino is a natural climate phenomenon and is not caused by climate change.
But scientists expect it will exacerbate the heat of a planet already warming from burning fossil fuels, while amping up weather extremes.
“El Nino is being supersized before our eyes,” said UN chief Antonio Guterres.
“The science leaves no room for doubt: the planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up. Sea surface temperatures are rising, temperatures keep climbing, and the world is in the danger zone of extreme weather.
“The race now is between rising risks and our commitment to take climate action and protect people. We must win that race.”
“This exceptional El Nino... has the potential to deliver a massive blow to communities and economies across the world,” said Saulo.
“We are already seeing disruption and devastation from droughts and floods, and we expect these impacts to increase as El Nino intensifies.”
She put disaster management authorities and climate-sensitive sectors like agriculture, health, energy and water on notice, saying there was “no time to lose” in getting ready.
El Nino typically takes place every two to seven years and lasts around nine to 12 months.
Conditions oscillate between El Nino and its opposite La Nina, with neutral conditions in between.
“Fueled by exceptionally warm ocean conditions across the tropical Pacific, El Nino is expected to strengthen further during the coming months to a very strong intensity,” the WMO said.
The UN agency classifies El Nino events as weak, moderate, strong or very strong -- meaning it is set to reach the highest level out of four.
The WMO said there was an “exceptionally high likelihood of nearly 100%” that El Nino will continue through to February.
El Nino can reshape weather and climate patterns thousands of kilometers away from the tropical Pacific.
Every El Nino is different, but major events often follow familiar patterns. This includes drought across parts of the Amazon, Indonesia and Australia, disrupted monsoons in India, and shifting rainfall throughout the tropics.
For September-November, WMO forecasts indicate an increased likelihood of above-normal temperatures “across almost all land areas,” alongside rainfall patterns showing a “pronounced and classic atmospheric response to the strong Pacific El Nino,” the UN’s weather and climate agency said.
The index which measures sea surface temperature anomalies in the central eastern equatorial Pacific has strengthened from an average 1.5°C above normal between May and July.
Weekly values between late July and mid-August ranged from around 2.2°C to 2.6°C above average, indicating continued El Nino intensification.
In some areas, subsurface ocean temperatures were more than 8°C above average during July and early August.

item.title: PM greets Hindu community on Janmashtami
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday greeted the members of the Hindu community in Bangladesh and around the world on the occasion of Janmashtami to be celebrated on Friday.
In a message, he urged people of all faiths to play a conscious and responsible role in maintaining social order, brotherhood and communal harmony and remain vigilant against any attempt to disrupt the peaceful atmosphere.
“I urge everyone to be vigilant so that no one can destroy this atmosphere of harmony,” he said.
The prime minister described Janmashtami as a significant religious occasion for Hindus and extended greetings to Hindu brothers and sisters and followers of Sanatan Dharma.
Referring to Hindu scriptures, he said Lord Krishna was born in Mathura on the eighth day of the waning fortnight of the lunar month during the reign of the tyrant King Kansa.
Krishna later ended Kansa’s oppressive rule, upheld righteousness and fought evil, he said.
The prime minister said Krishna’s life and teachings embody humanism, justice, equality and peace, while his ideals of devotion, human welfare and harmony continue to inspire people.
He said people of different religions and beliefs in Bangladesh have been practicing their faiths with mutual respect and harmony from ancient age.
He expressed hope that the ideals of Shri Krishna would further strengthen mutual harmony and brotherhood in the society.
The prime minister wished happiness, peace and prosperity for all on the occasion of Janmashtami.

item.title: Police: Five arrested with weapons over planned Banani robbery
item.description:
Five people have been arrested in Banani while allegedly preparing to commit a robbery, police said.
The arrestees were identified as Md Masud Rana, 29; Md Rajib Hawladar, 30; Hafizul Matbar, 24; Mohammad Shakil Hossain, 24; and Md Badal, 42.
Additional Police Commissioner (DB) Md Shafiqul Islam disclosed the information at a press conference at the DMP Media Centre on Thursday afternoon.
A foreign-made pistol, a magazine, a walkie-talkie, a pair of handcuffs bearing the Bangladesh Police emblem and other items allegedly intended for use in the robbery were recovered from them. Police also seized a Hiace microbus.
Gulshan Division of the Detective Branch received information around 9:30am that a group was preparing to carry out a robbery on Road No 4 in the Banani police station area, said the DMP official.
Acting on the tip-off, a 45-member DB team took position in the area and later conducted a raid in front of Khayer Palace on Road No 4, where the five suspects were arrested.
During the operation, police recovered a foreign-made pistol, a magazine, a walkie-talkie, a pair of handcuffs bearing the Bangladesh Police emblem, a roll of black adhesive tape, a shopping bag and the Hiace microbus.
The DB is interrogating the suspects to determine why they had gathered in the area and to establish details of their alleged robbery plan.
Investigators are also looking into whether the suspects are members of an organized criminal group, the source of the firearm, and whether they have previous criminal records or links to other offenses, police said.
Legal proceedings against the suspects are being initiated at Banani Police Station. Police are also continuing operations to identify and arrest others allegedly involved with the group.

Madrasa teacher arrested over rape allegation in Narayanganj
item.description:
Police have arrested a madrasa teacher in Fatullah, Narayanganj, over an allegation of raping a 17-year-old student.
The accused, Md Rafiqul Islam, 28, was arrested from Tahsinul Quran Madrasa in Muslim Nagar on Wednesday after local residents detained him and called the national emergency service 999.
Fatullah Model Police Station Inspector (Investigation) Anwar Hossain confirmed the arrest to Dhaka Tribune on Thursday afternoon.
He said the student’s father filed a case at the police station over the allegation. The student was sent to a hospital for a medical examination, while police have started investigating the case.
According to police, a resident of Muslim Nagar called 999 on Wednesday afternoon and reported that a teacher at the madrasa had allegedly raped a 17-year-old student.
The report prompted local residents to detain and beat the teacher, creating tension in the area. The emergency service subsequently informed Fatullah police station and requested police intervention.
A police team later went to the madrasa and arrested Rafiqul with the help of local residents before taking him to the police station.
Police sources said the student had completed Hifz, or memorization of the Quran, and enrolled at Tahsinul Quran Madrasa about a year ago to further improve his Quran memorization.
According to the allegations, Rafiqul had been sexually abusing the student for about a year by intimidating him.
The latest alleged assault took place on the night of August 31, after which the student fell ill, police sources said.
The student’s mother took him home for treatment. After learning about the alleged assault, she and local residents went to the madrasa and confronted the teacher.
Rafiqul is the son of the late Abdul Mannan of Barunda village under Tongibari police station in Munshiganj. He had been working as a teacher at Tahsinul Quran Madrasa in Muslim Nagar, Fatullah.
The information was provided in a statement issued by the national emergency service 999.

item.title: President urges expatriates to contribute to country’s development
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Thursday called upon Bangladeshi business people living abroad to further contribute to the country’s development by investing their money and making efforts to bring more foreign investment in the country.
The president made the call when a delegation of Bangladeshi expatriates living in the United Kingdom paid a courtesy call on him at Bangabhaban on Thursday afternoon, President’s Press Wing sources said.
Led by UK-based prominent businessman Kamal Uddin, the delegation congratulated Mirza Fakrul on assuming the office of the president.
The president gratefully recalled immense contribution of the expatriates to the movement for establishing democracy and justice in the country through investing their money, labour and intellect, saying “the country and its people would always remember your contribution and role.”
The president also expressed gratitude to the expatriates, noting that their remittances are one of the major driving forces of the country’s economy.
During the meeting, the delegation sought the president’s support to enhance business opportunities and civic facilities for them, including addressing the issue of harassment in the airports. They also urged for ensuring their voting rights in the country.
President Fakhrul Islam said, the government has already started working to resolve these problems and enhance civic facilities for the expatriates.
"Probashi Card has been introduced to ensure comprehensive service facilities and benefits for the expatriates,” he said.
He also urged expat Bangladeshis to invest more in the country, contribute to employment generation, education, healthcare, technology and skill development and other social welfare activities.
The delegation expressed interest in investing in the country.
President’s military secretary and press secretary were present at the meeting.

During the meeting, the two sides held an open and cordial exchange of views on issues of mutual interest and stressed the need to further strengthen the long-standing friendly and historic ties between Bangladesh and Malaysia, according to a press release.

item.title: Families descend on Nepal in search of missing tourists
item.description:
Desperate families of missing foreigners were clinging to hope as they combed hospitals and morgues in search of clues, a week after catastrophic floods tore through Nepal's Himalayan border region.
Outside Kathmandu's tourist police headquarters, Sanjeev Rai was trapped in agonising uncertainty.
The 53-year-old American flew to Nepal after learning that his wife, Jiwan Jyoti, was untraceable while returning from a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash, the sacred peak revered by Hindus and Buddhists.
"The day I arrived I said, let's find a helicopter, I'm going to look for her," Rai told AFP.
But Timure, the village in Rasuwa district where she was when disaster struck, remains inaccessible and dangerous.
"I feel desperate, it's been so many days," he said.
Jyoti, an engineer at Intel, had embarked on the journey as a spiritual quest and an adventure to mark her 50th birthday.
Now Rai says he has all but abandoned hope of finding her alive.
"I'm no longer counting on survivors. I just hope the DNA samples will match. I want to be able to mourn."
The August 26 flood has become one of the deadliest disasters to hit the Himalayan nation in recent years.
The huge wave of debris has killed more than 1,200 people and left more than 4,750 missing in Nepal and China's Tibet region, smashing towns, roads, bridges and multiple hydropower dams.
According to Nepali police, some 294 foreigners have been rescued, most of them Chinese and Indian nationals.
But 583 foreigners remain unaccounted for, many of them pilgrims who had spent months preparing for the demanding trek around Mount Kailash.
Among them are 77 pilgrims from spiritual leader Sadhguru's Isha Foundation, including Europeans, North Americans and Australians.
Several of their relatives have travelled to Kathmandu seeking answers, assisted by volunteers from the Foundation.
"We go to the Nepali police every day to get information on those who have been rescued. We examine photos... published by the police," said volunteer Arun Mehta.
Others spend their days visiting hospitals.
But all the members of the group, including three Nepali guides, remain missing till now, Mehta said.
"They had completed their pilgrimage around Mount Kailash and were going through immigration procedures" at the Gyirong border crossing with China when disaster struck, he said.
The foundation has provided identifying details to authorities, including distinctive snake-shaped rings and pendants worn by many pilgrims.
Nepal police began collecting DNA samples from relatives this week to build a database for identifying bodies, while families overseas will be able to submit samples in their home countries.
Thousands of kilometres away in Russia's far east, some relatives are making plans to join the search in Nepal.
From Yakutsk, the brother of missing musician Kirill Tretiakov, said he would travel to Nepal within days.
"For the moment, we have no information about Kirill," he told AFP. "We hope his group survived but ended up without any means of communication."
Tretiakov was travelling with a group of Russian and Ukrainian pilgrims organised by the travel agency Tashi Delek.
"We will start our search with the hospitals. No matter how long it takes, we will keep looking for him."
Another trek organiser Fishtail says it has lost contact with a group of 20 pilgrims, mostly Malaysians, who were travelling with guides and drivers.
"No one could escape, it was so sudden," said Nimsang Gurung, a sales representative with the company.
As search efforts continue, officials fear the disaster will have a big impact on tourism, a major source of revenue for the country.
"The tourism sector is going to suffer from this disaster," said Sunil Sharma of Nepal's National Tourism Agency, even though "only four districts" were directly affected.

item.title: HC dismisses rule over police security for housing project
item.description:
The High Court has dismissed a rule issued over police security for the implementation of the Purbachal Probashi Palli Limited housing project, after the state accused the writ petitioner of misusing the court’s interim order for personal gain.
Lawyers concerned confirmed the matter on Thursday.
The High Court bench of Justice Ahmed Sohel and Justice SM Iftekhar Uddin Mahmud pronounced the verdict.
According to the case documents, Mohammad Muhidur Rahman, managing director, and Habibur Rahman, chairman, established Purbachal Probashi Palli Limited in Dhaka’s Purbachal with funding from expatriates. The company was registered on December 31, 2009.
In 2011, the company filed a writ petition with the High Court seeking police security for its business activities.
Md Abdul Qayyum, the company’s project director, filed the petition under authority granted by the company. Nine people were made respondents, including the secretary of the Ministry of Home Affairs, the deputy commissioners and upazila nirbahi officers of Narayanganj and Narsingdi, the managing director of Purbachal American City Mohammad Abdullah Al Mamun, and the officers-in-charge of Rupganj and Narsingdi Sadar police stations.
Following the initial hearing on July 25, 2011, the High Court directed the OCs of Narsingdi Sadar and Rupganj police stations to provide necessary security for four months to prevent obstacles to the implementation of the project.
The court also issued a rule asking why the respondents’ failure to provide legal protection for the project should not be declared illegal and without lawful authority. It further asked why the respondents should not be directed to refrain from obstructing the lawful implementation of the project.
The company subsequently continued to operate its housing business by obtaining extensions of the four-month interim order from time to time over nearly 15 years.
Meanwhile, Sub-Inspector Ahsan Habib filed a response before the court on behalf of the OC of Rupganj police station, the ninth respondent in the case.
In the response filed on July 16, the state denied the allegations made in the writ petition. During the hearing, the state argued that the interim security order had been repeatedly extended and allegedly used for personal gain and fraudulent purposes for nearly 15 years.
The state told the court that the project was a privately owned commercial real estate and housing project whose legal approval and registration were themselves disputed.
It also said that in a case filed on September 11, 2024, under the anti-discrimination movement-related proceedings (GR Case No 154/2024), the project’s chairman Habibur Rahman and managing director Muhidur Rahman had been named as the first and 51st accused, respectively.
Despite this, the state argued that the project had continued to receive police security by relying on the 2011 High Court order.
The state further alleged that the project directors had forcibly taken possession of land belonging to farmers in several mouzas through fraud and forged documents. It said reports on the allegations had also been published in national newspapers.
The state argued that the original interim order in the writ had been misused to allegedly facilitate fraud and harass local landowners, while the institution itself lacked proper legal validity.
On these grounds, the state sought a penalty against the writ petitioner for allegedly filing the petition for personal gain.
After hearing both sides, the High Court dismissed the rule and delivered its verdict.
Following the verdict, the state’s lawyers said the writ petitioner had obtained a four-month interim order in 2011 and repeatedly extended it for nearly 15 years.
They alleged that the security order had been misused during this period and that the company had used it to pursue its own interests. They also alleged that the chairman and managing director, who were accused in a case related to the anti-discrimination movement, had used the High Court order to avoid arrest.
After considering the arguments, the High Court dismissed the rule issued in response to the writ petition.

item.title: Gold prices rise again
item.description:
After several rounds of price cuts, the Bangladesh Jewellers Association (Bajus) has raised gold prices again in the domestic market.
The price of 22-carat gold has been increased by Tk4,474 per bhori to Tk236,354, according to a Bajus announcement on Thursday.
The new price came into effect at 10am on Thursday.
Bajus said the new rates were set considering the overall market situation following an increase in the prices of acid gold and silver.
The decision was taken at a meeting of Bajus’s Standing Committee on Pricing and Price Monitoring on Thursday morning.
According to the new rates, 22-carat hallmarked gold costs Tk20,350 per gram, including VAT. The price of 21-carat gold has been set at Tk19,435 per gram, 18-carat gold at Tk16,685 per gram and traditional gold at Tk13,630 per gram.
Bajus has also increased the price of silver.
Under the new rates, 22-carat silver costs Tk440 per gram, 21-carat silver Tk425, 18-carat silver Tk365 and traditional silver Tk275 per gram.

item.title: 30 accused, including Sheikh Hasina, ordered to surrender
item.description:
The International Crimes Tribunal has ordered 30 accused, including ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, former army chief General Aziz Ahmed and former inspector general of police Benazir Ahmed, to surrender to the tribunal by September 16.
The order came in a case filed over alleged crimes against humanity in connection with the Shapla Chattar massacre.
A newspaper notice has been issued in this regard.
The judicial panel of Tribunal-2, headed by Chairman Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, passed the order on Thursday following a prosecution petition.
Earlier in the morning, the accused who are currently in custody were brought to the tribunal in prison vans amid tight security.
Eleven accused were scheduled to be produced before the tribunal on August 16. However, the prosecution sought more time, saying production warrants had not been issued against two of the accused and the non-execution reports (NERs) concerning those against whom arrest warrants had been issued had not been received.
The tribunal subsequently fixed Thursday for the proceedings.
On July 27, Tribunal-2 took cognizance of the formal complaint filed by the prosecution against 41 accused. It also issued arrest warrants against the absconding accused and ordered those in custody to be produced before the tribunal.
The case involves two charges. The first relates to the alleged killing of 32 people at Shapla Chattar in Dhaka’s Motijheel on May 5, 2013, during a Hefazat-e-Islam rally.
The second charge relates to alleged killings in different parts of the country, including the deaths of 20 people in Siddhirganj, Narayanganj, on May 6, 2013.

item.title: Dhaka air quality remains ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 10th among the world’s cities with the worst air quality on Thursday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 106 at 9:42am.
According to the AQI scale, the city's air quality was classified as “unhealthy for sensitive groups”, posing health risks to children, older adults, and people with heart or lung diseases, while the general public is mostly unaffected.
Kuching in Malaysia topped the global pollution list with an AQI of 274, followed by Kampala in Uganda with 16q and Jakarta in Indonesia with 158.
An AQI reading of 101 to 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", and anything above 301 is categorized as "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides a daily indication of air quality by measuring the level of pollution and its potential impact on human health.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants — particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long faced serious air pollution problems, with air quality generally deteriorating during the winter months and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution contributes to around 7 million deaths worldwide every year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Rangamati hanging bridge submerged as Kaptai Lake water rises
item.description:
Rangamati’s iconic hanging bridge has been submerged as the water level of Kaptai Lake rose sharply following days of heavy rain and upstream runoff from the hills.
The popular tourist attraction is now off-limits to visitors, leaving hundreds of tourists disappointed and dealing a blow to the local tourism industry.
The Bangladesh Parjatan Corporation has suspended access to the bridge for safety reasons. Red flags have been placed at the entrance and bamboo barriers installed to prevent visitors from entering the submerged structure.
Tourists arriving from different parts of the country said they were disappointed after finding the bridge underwater.
“I had wanted to see Rangamati’s Hanging Bridge up close for a long time. But after coming here, I found that the bridge was submerged. I could not even take a picture. It was really disappointing,” said Mohammad Ashraful Islam, who travelled from Dhaka with his family.
The closure has also affected businesses that depend on tourist arrivals.
More than a hundred engine-powered boats are reportedly lying idle at the local boat terminal as tourists have stopped coming for trips on Kaptai Lake.
Shops selling traditional clothing, textiles and handicrafts are also struggling due to the sharp decline in customers, with some traders saying their daily sales have fallen to almost zero.
Mohammad Fakhrul Islam, leaseholder of the local Boat Owners’ Association, said the current period is crucial for their livelihoods.
“The tourist rush during this time of year helps support our families throughout the year. But since the bridge was submerged, our income has completely stopped. If the situation continues, we will have to bear significant financial losses,” he said.
Hotel owner Mohammad Sumon Mia said the hanging bridge is one of the main attractions for visitors to Rangamati.
“Many tourists come to Rangamati to visit the bridge. Since it was submerged, hotel bookings have been cancelled every day. The decline in tourist arrivals is causing losses for hotels, motels and restaurants,” he said.
Alok Bikash Chakma, manager of Rangamati Tourism Corporation, said the bridge was submerged after the water level of Kaptai Lake rose due to heavy rainfall and runoff from the hills.
“The bridge is currently under 4-6 inches of water. For the safety of visitors, we have put up red flags and blocked access with bamboo barriers,” he said.
He said authorities hope the water level will recede within a few days, after which the restrictions on visitors will be lifted.
Meanwhile, Rangamati District Council Chairman Dipan Talukdar Dipu said a survey for the construction of a new bridge had already been conducted.
“We hope construction of a new, modern bridge at a higher elevation will begin soon. Once completed, the new bridge will help attract more tourists to Rangamati,” he said.

item.title: Heavy rain paralyses life in Rajshahi
item.description:
Heavy rain triggered severe waterlogging in several parts of Rajshahi city and Chapainawabganj town causing widespread suffering for residents and disrupting normal movement.
The Rajshahi Weather Office recorded 99.4 millimetres of rainfall on Wednesday morning, the highest rainfall recorded in the city this season.
Several major roads and lanes were inundated, including areas in front of the Divisional Commissioner’s Office and Rajshahi Medical College Hospital, as well as Barnali intersection, Hetemkha and Laxmipur. In some areas, knee-deep water covered the roads.
Motorcycles and auto-rickshaws became stranded in the water, while office-goers, students and pedestrians struggled to move through the flooded streets. The situation caused traffic disruptions and made it difficult for people to reach their workplaces, educational institutions and other destinations.
Although the water began to recede after the rain stopped, normal movement remained disrupted throughout the morning.
Anwar Hossain, a resident of the Barnali intersection area, said even a short spell of rain often leaves roads flooded.
“Rajshahi is known as one of the country’s cleanest and most beautiful cities, but even a little rain causes waterlogging, making it difficult to move around. The drains are not cleaned regularly, which makes the problem worse,” he said.
College student Anika Tabassum said waterlogging frequently creates problems for students.
“Even moderate rain makes it difficult to attend classes. Road water often mixes with waste from the drains, creating an unbearable stench,” she said.
The latest downpour has once again exposed Rajshahi’s persistent waterlogging problem, leaving residents to suffer from flooded roads, traffic disruption and foul-smelling stagnant water.
Mostafa Kamal Hossain, deputy director of the Department of Agricultural Extension in Rajshahi, also said rainfall at this stage creates favourable conditions for better growth and yield of Aman rice. He said adequate water is particularly important during the flowering and grain-forming stages of the crop for achieving a good yield.
Rainwater has entered homes, government offices, educational institutions, student hostels and other establishments in Chapainawabganj town. Several roads have been submerged under ankle-deep water, while water has risen to knee level in some areas.
Light rain began on Tuesday evening before turning into heavy downpours around midnight. As a result, several areas of the municipality, including Arambagh, Shantir Mor, Batenkhan’s Mor, Old Market, New Market and Udayan Mor, have been flooded.
Several roads have become nearly impassable due to the waterlogging. In some areas, residents have been temporarily confined to their homes as water accumulated in front of their houses. Parts of kitchens and tube-wells have also gone underwater, while water has entered several student hostels.
Local residents blamed inadequate drainage facilities, poor maintenance of existing drains and unplanned urbanisation for the recurring waterlogging in the municipality. They said even moderate rainfall often causes several areas to become flooded.
Safi, a resident of Arambagh, said, “Even when there was heavy rain in the past, water never entered our homes. This time, our houses have been flooded. We are struggling to protect our belongings. We urge the municipal authorities to take immediate measures to address the problem.”
Faisal, a student of Nawabganj Government College, said, “Rainwater entered our hostel and soaked all our books and notebooks. We also had to struggle to drain the water from our room.”
Tawfiqul Islam, executive engineer of Chapainawabganj Municipality, said, “It rained continuously from 9pm to 9am, causing several parts of the municipality to become waterlogged. The water will gradually recede.
