item.title: Minister Tuku hospitalised, condition stable
item.description:
Power, Energy, and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood Tuku is in stable condition after being admitted to hospital with fever, shortness of breath and a cough, hospital authorities said on Wednesday.
However, a medical board has advised him to remain in hospital for a few more days for further treatment and close monitoring.
The 76-year-old minister was taken to the emergency department of Ibrahim Cardiac Hospital and Research Institute in the capital at around 9:40pm on Tuesday after developing fever, shortness of breath and a cough.
Initial examinations found that he was experiencing shortness of breath and had low blood oxygen levels. He was subsequently admitted to the Coronary Care Unit (CCU).
In a statement, the hospital said doctors began treatment after reviewing the results of blood tests and a chest X-ray, which indicated pneumonia. A three-member medical board was immediately formed to oversee his treatment.
On Wednesday morning, a broader medical board comprising specialists from different disciplines was formed. His treatment is continuing in line with the board's recommendations, while further tests are being conducted as necessary.
Tuku has a history of diabetes and hypertension and recently underwent a procedure in Bangkok to have a stent placed in a coronary artery.
The medical board said he remains physically stable but will require a few more days in hospital for comprehensive treatment and close observation.

item.title: 5,000 US sailors arrive in Thailand after months at sea
item.description:
Around 5,000 US sailors and Marines arrived in Thailand on Wednesday for their first port call in nine months, after concerns over conditions on board sparked debate back home over President Donald Trump’s war with Iran.
The arrival of the USS Abraham Lincoln has made businesses in nearby Pattaya hopeful of a major windfall, but has also drawn renewed scrutiny of the resort town’s reputation as a hub for sex tourism.
The aircraft carrier docked in the port of Laem Chabang, south of Bangkok and a half-hour drive from Pattaya, for five days of rest and recreation after 286 days at sea, most recently in the Middle East.
“We’re all very excited, it should get quite lively,” said Anthony “AJ” Jones, a 60-year-old musician from New Zealand who performs every night at M’s Mojito beach bar in Pattaya.
A banner outside the bar reads: “Welcome all US military personnel. Thank you for your service.”
“It’s been the talk of the town for the past few days... it will be a boon for businesses,” Jones told AFP, saying he was planning to perform some American classics to entertain the sailors.
With the world watching and an eye on the potential for trouble, Pattaya authorities have reportedly barred the sailors from the most notorious of the city’s streets, which are filled with hostess bars and semi-naked women.
The visitors will also be unable to engage in water sports, such as jet-skiing, and to take advantage of Thailand’s lax cannabis laws, according to Pattaya’s mayor, Poramase Ngampiches.
Authorities recently cracked down on sex workers in the city, Poramase told AFP, but insisted this was routine, denying it was linked to the Americans.
Security has also been stepped up.
“Our arrival in Laem Chabang provides a well-deserved opportunity for our sailors and Marines to rest and recharge,” Rear Admiral Robert Loughran, commander of the US Carrier Strike Group 3, said in a statement.
The Lincoln’s commanding officer, Captain Dan Keeler, added that its first port visit of the “historic deployment” would allow “our crew to enjoy this beautiful and historic country.”
The huge nuclear-powered carrier arrived early on Wednesday morning at Laem Chabang, with dozens of warplanes lined up on its flight deck, AFP reporters saw.
It was the first dry-land call since leaving California in November for duty in the South China Sea. The carrier was rerouted to the Middle East before US-Israeli attacks on Iran began in February.
Reports of deteriorating living conditions and poor mental health on board -- including attempted suicides -- made headlines in the United States and provoked criticism of the ongoing conflict.
Democratic lawmakers have called for an investigation into conditions on board following reports of food shortages, broken plumbing and mental health crises.
But Trump has dismissed the concerns.
“A small number of mental health cases were treated with no loss of life,” acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao said in mid-August, blaming the media for “trying to paint our warriors as victims.”
The carrier was replaced in the Middle East by the USS George Washington, which had been in Japan.
That ship in turn will be relieved by the USS Theodore Roosevelt, which will sail from San Diego in the coming weeks, according to the private military association the US Naval Institute.
Pattaya comes to life at night and, in the hours before the US sailors arrived, the city appeared largely peaceful, with masseuses sitting idly outside their shops waiting for customers, and a few foreign tourists sunbathing on the beach.
One tailor shop posted a sign in its window offering clothes “Specially for US Navy -- Ready in 24 hours.”
“We’ll give them a special offer, good quality and a quick service -- 24 hours or even 12 hours,” said the owner, Islam.
“All of Pattaya is excited.”
The mayor said buses have been laid on to transport the sailors from the ship to Pattaya and back until the carrier departs on Sunday.
“Our preparations will focus on safety and ensuring fair pricing, so we don’t take advantage of them,” Poramase said in a video posted on Facebook.

item.title: Iran attacks US sites after American strikes, wedding deaths
item.description:
Iran launched a wave of attacks on US sites across the Middle East on Wednesday as violence surged after an extensive American bombardment and the deaths of four people at an Iranian wedding party.
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards announced attacks on US bases in Jordan, the UAE, Kuwait, Bahrain and Iraq’s autonomous Kurdistan region, in the six-month conflict’s heaviest exchange in weeks.
US President Donald Trump had warned earlier of “much harder and higher” attacks if Iran retaliated to the US strikes, which Iran’s military and state media said killed 18 people.
The renewed attacks deepen the impasse in the war, where Iran maintains a stranglehold on the Strait of Hormuz oil export route with the US pressing a counter-blockade of Iranian ports.
In the latest strikes, the Iranian Red Crescent said on Tuesday that four people including a child were killed and more than 50 people were wounded by a US attack while attending a wedding in Iran’s south.
A video shared by an Iranian government account showed extensive debris and damage at what it said was the wedding site in Sirik following a US strike, with people heard screaming in the background.
Iran’s top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf lashed out at the United States, calling it “Satan.”
“If a power acts like Satan, picks targets like Satan, and kills like Satan, it’s Satan. Shields a junior Satan that does the same? It’s THE Great Satan,” he posted on X.
The US military did not address the wedding strike directly.
US Central Command (Centcom) spokesman Tim Hawkins said “the US military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC,” referring to Iran’s Revolutionary Guards.
The latest round of fighting began when Washington hit Iranian targets on Sunday, the first known strikes in several weeks.
Tehran’s forces then targeted US troops in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates, and projectiles struck two oil tankers in unclaimed attacks.
Trump said Sunday’s “large and powerful” strikes were “in retaliation for the Iranians’ failed attempt at adding sea mines to the Strait” and “the Iranians shooting eight missiles, all successfully knocked down, at our Military Base in Jordan.”
More US strikes came on Tuesday, with Iranian state television reporting explosions in the country’s south along the Hormuz Strait and on an island in the Gulf, and that US forces hit an airport in the southern province of Kerman.
Seven people were killed and eight others wounded in a missile attack in the southern Khuzestan province, Irna reported.
The IRGC said four members of its aerospace force were killed in a US strike in the western province of Kermanshah, and three paramilitaries died in an attack on Lavan island in the Gulf.
Iran’s Guards said their retaliatory strikes included “a coordinated missile and drone attack on US bases in Erbil” that destroyed a maintenance center, warehouses and the “guidance system of a US surveillance aerostat,” according to a statement carried by the state-run Irna news agency.
An AFP journalist reported hearing explosions near Erbil’s airport, which hosts coalition troops.
The Guards also announced a ballistic missile attack on a US Marine training camp in Jordan on the Gulf of Aqaba, near the borders with Israel and Saudi Arabia, according to Iran’s Tasnim news agency.
In the oil-rich Gulf, air raid sirens rang out across Bahrain and also Kuwait, where authorities said an Iranian drone set off a blaze at a residential complex. The fire was extinguished with no casualties, they said.
Revolutionary Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebi had warned on X that Washington “will regret its new attacks,” saying that “severe punishment awaits the aggressors.”
The Middle East war began in late February with US-Israeli attacks on Iran that killed its supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
A fragile ceasefire between the United States and Iran collapsed after attacks on commercial ships in the Hormuz Strait, through which one-fifth of world oil supplies flowed before the war.
Incidents in the strait have continued, and Iran’s Guards said Wednesday that two oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines “at the urging of the US military to transit via an illegal route.”
Trump warned on his Truth Social platform Tuesday that if Iran retaliated to US attacks, “they will be hit again at a much harder and higher level, but it will not be the biggest attack of them all.”
“There will be very little left of the Islamic Republic of Iran!” he wrote.
Despite the diplomatic deadlock, Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian vowed on Tuesday to match any US move to return to a deal aimed at ending the war.
He also warned that a return by the United States to “a policy of pressure and threats could derail the path of diplomacy.”

item.title: Berger Paints Bangladesh, NDE Steel Structures sign two agreements
item.description:
Berger Paints Bangladesh Limited and NDE Steel Structures Limited have recently signed two separate agreements.
Under the first agreement, NDE Steel Structures Limited will undertake the steel structure works for key infrastructure at Berger Paints’ third manufacturing facility under construction at the National Special Economic Zone (NSEZ) in Mirsarai, Chittagong.
The project will further strengthen Berger’s manufacturing and supply chain capabilities while supporting its future business growth.
The new facility will significantly enhance Berger’s production capacity to meet the growing demand for paints and coatings in Bangladesh.
At the same time, the project is expected to create new employment opportunities, contribute to the development of local skills, and support the industrial and economic development of the Mirsarai region.
With its strategic location and world-class infrastructure, the National Special Economic Zone in Mirsarai is already emerging as one of the country’s key industrial destinations.
Berger’s new investment in the zone is expected to further contribute to the development of Bangladesh’s manufacturing and industrial sectors.
In addition, under the second agreement signed between the two companies, NDE Steel Structures Limited will exclusively use Berger Paints Bangladesh Limited’s products and solutions across its construction projects.
The agreement is expected to further strengthen the long-term business relationship between the two companies and expand the use of quality products and solutions across the industrial sector.
On behalf of Berger Paints Bangladesh Limited, the ceremony was graced by Mohsin Habib Chowdhury, chief executive officer & managing director; Abul Kasem Mohammad Sadeque Nawaj, chief business officer; Salahuddin Ahmed, chief marketing officer; Raquibul Alam, chief supply chain officer; Mahfuzul Haque, head of CAPEX and S&IM Procurement; and members of Berger's industrial sales team and the third factory project team were also present on the occasion.
Representing NDE Steel Structures Ltd, the attendees included Imran Mustafiz, managing director; Md Shamsuzzaman, chief executive officer; and Md Aminul Islam, deputy general manager, sales & marketing.
Commenting on the partnership, a senior official of Berger Paints Bangladesh Limited said: “We are delighted to partner with NDE Steel Structures Limited for this important project at our upcoming facility in Mirsarai. This investment reflects Berger’s long-standing commitment to innovation, manufacturing excellence, and sustainable growth in Bangladesh. We are confident that NDE’s expertise and capabilities will enable us to successfully complete the project on schedule while maintaining the highest standards of quality.”
A representative from NDE Steel Structures Limited said: “We are proud to be entrusted with the construction of the Water Base Production Building, Silo, and FG Warehouse for Berger Paints Bangladesh Limited’s Mirsarai facility. Drawing on our experience in industrial and steel structure projects, we are committed to completing the project safely, on schedule, and to the highest standards of quality and engineering excellence.”

item.description:
The Ministry of Commerce has approved a Tk5-per-litre increase in the retail price of bottled soybean oil, raising the price of a one-litre bottle to Tk204 from Tk199.
The approval was granted on Wednesday following a request from edible oil traders for a price adjustment. The traders had initially sought a Tk10 increase per litre.
The decision was made at a meeting between Commerce Minister Khandaker Abdul Muqtadir and edible oil traders at the ministry.
Speaking at an emergency press briefing after the meeting, Commerce Secretary Md Ataur Rahman Khan said rising international edible oil prices and higher transportation costs had prompted importers to seek a price hike.
“Traders had sought a higher increase, but the government has adjusted the price by Tk5 per litre,” he said.
He added that there was currently no shortage of edible oil in the market and that the decision was taken after considering the overall market situation.
Asked whether prices could rise again ahead of Ramadan, the commerce secretary said any further adjustment would depend on market conditions at the time.

item.title: Dhaka ranks 11th globally for poor air quality
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 11th among the world’s cities with the worst air quality on Wednesday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 105 at 9:35am.
According to the AQI scale, the city's air quality was classified as “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups”, poses health risks to children, older adults, and people with heart or lung diseases, while the general public is mostly unaffected.
Kuching in Malaysia topped the global pollution list with an AQI of 346, followed by Kinshasa in the Democratic Republic of Congo with 168 and Kolkata in India with 164.
An AQI reading of 101 to 150 is considered ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’, while 151 to 200 is classified as ‘unhealthy’. A reading between 201 and 300 is considered ‘very unhealthy’, and anything above 301 is categorized as ‘hazardous’, posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides a daily indication of air quality by measuring the level of pollution and its potential impact on human health.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants — particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long faced serious air pollution problems, with air quality generally deteriorating during the winter months and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution contributes to around 7 million deaths worldwide every year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Shama Obaed: Gor’s Boeing purchase remarks may have referred to an earlier deal
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Tuesday said US Special Envoy Sergio Gor’s remarks about Bangladesh purchasing more Boeing aircraft might have referred to the country’s previously concluded aircraft deal.
She made the remarks while talking to reporters at the ministry of foreign affairs.
US Special Envoy for South and Central Asia and Ambassador to India Sergio Gor recently said Bangladesh has committed billions of dollars to buy additional Boeing aircraft from the United States under a new deal between Dhaka and Washington.
"Just this week, President Trump and the Prime Minister of Bangladesh (Tarique Rahman) made another incredible deal, with Bangladesh committing to spend billions of dollars to buy more Boeing aircraft, significantly increasing their initial order," Gor said in a post on X on Sunday night.
In April, Bangladesh signed a deal with US aircraft manufacturer Boeing to buy 14 planes for its national carrier Biman Bangladesh Airlines, the two sides announced - the airline’s biggest-ever order, in a deal valued at $3.7 billion.
Gor visited Bangladesh from July 30-August 1 and met with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman to discuss the political and economic dynamics shaping Bangladesh-US relations.
Meanwhile, State Minister Shama said the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) will deepen cooperation with Bangladesh to strengthen parliamentary democracy and enhance lawmakers’ capacity as the country moves forward with a young and newly constituted parliament.
“The IPU will work with Bangladesh and extend its cooperation to further strengthen democracy in the country,” she told journalists at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs after a meeting with visiting IPU Secretary General Anda Filip.
She said the IPU delegation is observing Bangladesh’s current political and democratic situation and has interacted with lawmakers from both the ruling and opposition parties, as well as women parliamentarians.
The delegation is examining how parliamentary democracy is functioning in Bangladesh following the country’s return to democratic governance after years of political transition, she said.
Shama said the IPU views Bangladesh’s new parliament positively, particularly because of the presence of a significant number of young and first-time lawmakers.
“Bangladesh now has a young and new parliament. Many of its members are first-time MPs and comparatively young, with greater representation of youth in parliament. They view this very positively,” she said.
The state minister said her discussion with the IPU Secretary General also covered ways to enhance the skills and institutional capacity of Bangladeshi lawmakers and strengthen their engagement with parliamentarians across the world.
She said Bangladesh is interested in greater participation by its lawmakers in the IPU’s capacity-building and training programs, including those held in Geneva.
The two sides also discussed democracy, human rights, peace and stability, Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), women’s empowerment, gender equality and climate resilience - areas Shama described as priorities for the government.
“On behalf of the government, I expressed our commitment to engaging more closely with the Inter-Parliamentary Union,” she said.
The IPU is scheduled to hold a conference in Tanzania next month, where Bangladesh’s Speaker and parliament members are expected to participate, she added.
Filip arrived in Dhaka on Sunday night and is scheduled to leave Bangladesh on September 2.

item.title: Land dispute leaves Sreepur bridge idle for 3 years
item.description:
Three years after a Tk18.96 crore bridge was completed over the Dhatri River in Sreepur, Gazipur, local residents are still unable to use it as a land acquisition dispute has stalled construction of its approach road.
Around 30 families living in 20 households are affected by the acquisition of 1 acre and 37 decimals of land needed to build the road on the northern side of the bridge.
Six families have already received compensation, while 24 others are still waiting for their payments.
The affected families allege that local resident Mobarak Hossain filed a court case claiming ownership of the acquired land and demanding Tk50 lakh from them to withdraw the case.
Protesting the alleged harassment and extortion, more than 100 residents from the affected families formed a human chain on Tuesday near Paital Bari, beside the northern side of the bridge at Baromi Bazar.
They demanded that the authorities ensure compensation is paid to the genuine landowners and investigate the alleged extortion.
Affected residents Sohel Mia, Faruk Mia and Manzurul said compensation should be paid to whoever legally owns the acquired land.
“We want the administration to ensure that genuine landowners receive their rightful compensation and that no one can intimidate or illegally demand money from them,” they said.
Another affected resident, Liton Mia, said they were facing various complications and pressure in receiving compensation for their land.
“We urge the administration to closely monitor the matter so that no one can take undue advantage of the situation,” he said.
Mobarak Hossain and Hridoy, who have been accused by the affected families, acknowledged that they currently have no structures on the acquired land. However, they claimed they owned property there but were not currently in possession of it.
They said ownership of the land and entitlement to compensation should be determined based on documents and the law. They denied the allegations of demanding money or harassing the affected families.
The Roads and Highways Department acquired 1 acre and 37 decimals of land for the approach road. Of the 13 plots involved, 12 are recorded as privately owned, while one is listed under Khas Khatian No 1 as government land.
The bridge, measuring around 98 metres in length, was constructed by the Roads and Highways Department at a cost of Tk18.96 crore to ease public suffering in the area. Construction began in January 2021 and was completed in September 2023.
However, the approach road remains incomplete due to the land acquisition dispute, leaving the bridge unusable nearly three years after its completion.
When contacted, Sreepur Upazila Assistant Commissioner (Land) Nahid Niaz Shishir said he was unaware of the matter.
“I know nothing about this issue. You can speak to the UNO for details,” he said.
Despite several attempts to contact Sreepur Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Nahid Bhuiyan on his official phone number, he did not answer.

item.title: 1,000 Rohingya to receive skills training under China-backed program
item.description:
A skills development program for 1,000 Rohingya has been launched at Camp 11 in Ukhiya, Cox’s Bazar, with support from the Embassy of the People’s Republic of China in Bangladesh.
National humanitarian development organization Impact Initiative inaugurated the program, titled “Sustainable Opportunities for Livelihoods, Advancement and Resilience (SOLAR),” at the Multipurpose Building of Rohingya Camp 11 on Tuesday.
Md Shariful Islam, deputy secretary and Camp-in-Charge of Camp 11, attended the inauguration as the chief guest, while Impact Initiative Chief Executive Officer Md Enayet Hossain chaired the event.
Under the SOLAR initiative, 325 participants will receive practical, market-oriented technical training in tailoring and dressmaking, block printing and batik, mobile phone servicing, gas burner repair and climate-smart agriculture.
Another 675 participants will receive soft-skills training focused on communication, teamwork, problem-solving, workplace behavior and other essential life and employability skills.
Speaking at the inauguration, Shariful Islam said skills development and practical livelihood training could play an important role in strengthening the capacity and self-reliance of the Rohingya community.
“Initiatives such as SOLAR will help participants develop practical skills and prepare themselves for future livelihood opportunities,” he said.
Enayet Hossain said Impact Initiative was creating opportunities for the Rohingya community to develop practical and market-relevant skills with support from the Chinese Embassy.
“Through the SOLAR initiative, we aim to strengthen their capacity, resilience and prospects for sustainable livelihoods,” he said.
The initiative aims to complement humanitarian assistance with skills development and livelihood-focused interventions, helping Rohingya community members build practical capacities and improve their prospects for self-reliance amid prolonged displacement.
With support from the Chinese Embassy and implementation by Impact Initiative, the program is expected to expand skills and livelihood opportunities for Rohingya community members in the camp.

item.title: Aromatic rice prices double in Rajshahi, consumers count the cost
item.description:
The price of aromatic rice has nearly doubled in Rajshahi over the past six months, with wholesale prices now reaching Tk200 per kilogram, putting the traditionally popular rice beyond the reach of many consumers.
Farmers and traders say they have never seen such a sharp rise in aromatic rice prices. Rice that sold for around Tk100 per kg six months ago now costs Tk180-200 in wholesale markets, while retail prices are even higher.
Traders blame the surge largely on exports, while other market players point to lower production, early stockpiling by large millers and rising processing and transport costs.
Three leading companies exported a combined 1,530 tonnes of rice in the 2025-26 fiscal year. Much of the country's aromatic rice is produced from BRRI-34, commonly known as Chinigura paddy. Rice currently on the market comes mainly from paddy harvested during the last Aman season.
The last production season was affected by severe heatwaves and a lack of rainfall in parts of northern Bangladesh, reducing aromatic paddy yields. At the same time, large rice processors bought paddy at relatively high prices early in the season and stocked it, creating supply pressure for smaller mills and the open market.
Aromatic rice also requires specialised processing and polishing. Higher electricity bills, milling expenses and transport costs have further increased production and distribution costs.
The price increases have changed the way many families buy the rice, traditionally associated with pulao, biryani and special occasions.
In Rajshahi's Saheb Bazar, open Chinigura rice now sells for Tk140-145 per kg, up from Tk115-120 a few months ago. Packaged Chinigura from leading brands has risen from Tk135-140 to Tk160-170. Local Kalijira rice has increased from Tk120-125 to around Tk150, while Dinajpur's Kataribhog now sells for Tk95-105, about Tk15 higher than before.
For lower-income households, the increase means cutting back on a food once reserved for special occasions.
Mohammad Azad, an employee shopping in Saheb Bazar, said: “Aromatic rice is not an everyday food, but the price has risen so much that even buying it for a family occasion has become difficult. We want to know why the price is increasing so quickly.”
Housewife Selina Parvin said she needed Chinigura rice for her daughter's birthday, when relatives would visit.
“Open Chinigura now costs Tk145 per kg. With the money I previously spent on four kilos, I cannot even buy three kilos now,” she said.
Restaurant owners are also feeling the pressure. Mohammad Golap Sardar, who runs a restaurant in Kumarpara, said he bought pulao rice for Tk130 per kg six months ago. The price has now reached Tk200, but he has been unable to raise the price of pulao accordingly.
Ashok Prasad, owner of AP Chawal Bhandar-1 in Saheb Bazar, said prices began rising after Eid-ul-Azha.
“The price has increased by around Tk100 per kg. This is unprecedented. Rice is being exported, and that is why prices are rising. If exports are stopped, prices will come down,” he said.
Wholesale trader Jasim Uddin of Kadirganj said he now buys aromatic rice from company warehouses at around Tk200 per kg. After adding transport costs and his commission, he said, selling below that price is impossible.
He said he was fined Tk10,000 by the Directorate of National Consumers' Right Protection after officials found him selling pulao rice at Tk200 per kg.
Jasim said he had stopped stocking the rice and believed prices could fall by around Tk50 per kg if exports were suspended.
Trader Rajib Hossain said higher prices were hurting sellers as well, as customers were buying less.
“Customers who once bought five or 10 kilos now often buy just one or two kilos,” he said.
Meanwhile, farmer Asfakuzzaman Babu of Godagari's Keshabpur said he cultivated aromatic paddy on two bighas but sold his entire harvest six months ago.
“If prices remain this high, I will cultivate more aromatic paddy next season,” he said.
Rajshahi chapter of the Consumers Association of Bangladesh (CAB) General Secretary Golam Mostafa Mamun said. “ We are monitoring the market to solve the situation.”

item.title: Four die from electrocution in Chuadanga
item.description:
Four people including a couple died from electrocution in separate incidents in Sadar and Damurhuda upazilas of Chuadanga district on Tuesday.
Liton Ali, a farmer and his wife Lipa Khatun of Kaliabakri village in Damurhuda upazila died after being electrocuted as he came in contact with live electric wire while cutting grass at an electric machine for cattle around 3 pm.
Dr Mostafizur Rahman, a duty officer of Damurhuda Upazila Health Complex, said “We found the two people dead. There were signs on their bodies indicating electrocution. We initially believe they died from electric shock.”
Meanwhile, Shafiqul Islam alias Baru, 48, son of Sirajul Islam of Shantipara in Darshana municipality, was killed by electrocution while attempting to steal an electric motor from a house in Loknathpur of Damurhuda upazila, said Sheikh Mesbah Uddin, Officer-in-Charge of Damurhuda Police Station.
Police said Shafiqul entered the house of Keramat Ali intending to steal the motor. At one point, he was electrocuted while cutting the power connection wires of an electric motor near the house’s water tap.
Necessary legal procedures are underway, said OC.
In Sadar upazila, Nasir Uddin, 40, an easy-bike driver and son of Gias Uddin, died as he came in contact with live electric wire while charging his easy-bike at Alukdia village in Sadar upazila around 12:30 pm, said Maruf Hossain, Officer-in-Charge of Sadar Police Station.

item.title: Shama Obaed: Bangladesh to consider public interest before joining any alliance
item.description:
Bangladesh will consider the interests of its people before deciding whether to join any multilateral alliance or pact, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam has said.
She said any such decision would be assessed in line with the government’s “Bangladesh First” foreign policy, with priority given to the benefits it could bring to Bangladesh and its people.
“We will certainly assess any multilateral body or pact in line with our current ‘Bangladesh First’ foreign policy. Before joining, we will consider the benefits for Bangladesh and its people,” she said.
“We have not received any formal invitation yet. Let’s see. The matter remains open for consideration and will be reviewed. It will take some time,” she added.
Shama made the remarks while speaking to journalists after a meeting with the secretary-general of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Tuesday.
She said the IPU delegation was observing Bangladesh’s current political and democratic situation.
“They have spoken with MPs from various opposition parties and the ruling party, as well as women MPs. Yesterday (Monday), they also visited the July Museum,” she said.
According to the state minister, the delegation came at a time when democracy had returned to Bangladesh after many years and was now functioning effectively and from a position of strength.
“The meeting with me was very good. On behalf of the government, we expressed our commitment to greater engagement with the IPU,” she said.
She added that the IPU will hold a conference next month, which will be attended by Bangladesh’s Speaker and members of parliament.

item.title: Adviser: Dhaka loadshedding to ease rural power crisis
item.description:
The government has decided to coordinate loadshedding in Dhaka and other major cities to reduce prolonged power outages in rural areas, Prime Minister’s Information and Broadcasting Adviser Dr Zahed Ur Rahman said on Tuesday.
He said electricity saved through loadshedding in areas under the Dhaka Power Distribution Company Limited (DPDC) and Dhaka Electric Supply Company Limited (Desco) is being redistributed to rural areas and other parts of the country based on demand.
The adviser made the remarks at the government’s weekly briefing at the Department of Information.
“Previously, relatively uninterrupted power was supplied to the capital and major cities, while rural and remote areas bore the brunt of loadshedding. The current government has decided to move away from that approach and share the burden of the crisis more evenly,” he said.
He said demand for electricity remains high in major cities because of their economic activity. Nevertheless, power is being redistributed on the prime minister’s instructions to reduce prolonged and frequent outages in rural areas.
Zahed Ur Rahman attributed the current power shortage to the energy crisis, sudden mechanical failures at power plants, maintenance work, limitations in the transmission grid and rapidly rising demand.
“As a result of coordinated loadshedding in areas under DPDC and Desco in Dhaka, power supply to industries and important consumer groups outside the capital is improving. At the same time, the pressure of prolonged outages in rural areas is being reduced to some extent,” he said.
“We are in a crisis. Everyone will have to bear the brunt of it to some extent. However, we do not think this hardship will last long,” the adviser said.
He also clarified the finance minister’s recent statement that it could take two years to fully resolve the country’s power and energy crisis.
“This does not mean the current level of loadshedding will continue for two years. If the recent mechanical and energy supply problems are resolved, the situation will return to its previous level within a relatively short time,” he said.
However, he said ensuring a reliable long-term power and energy supply would require new LNG infrastructure, domestic gas exploration and expanded power generation capacity.
Noting that establishing new floating storage and regasification units (FSRUs) would also take time, he said: “If these projects are implemented, LNG import capacity will increase.”
Zahed Ur Rahman also highlighted the geopolitical situation in the Middle East as a major risk to energy security.
LNG prices have already risen significantly in the international market, he said, warning that a further deterioration of the situation could make it difficult for the government to manage the energy crisis.

item.title: Zahed: Battery-powered rickshaws not banned, licensing policy in works
item.description:
The government is preparing a comprehensive policy to regulate battery-powered three-wheeled e-rickshaws, including provisions for vehicle standards, safety, driver licences, registration and designated routes.
Prime Minister’s Information and Broadcasting Adviser Dr Zahed Ur Rahman disclosed the plan at the government’s weekly briefing on Tuesday.
He said a meeting was held on August 30 at the Local Government Department with stakeholders to discuss the operation and management of battery-powered three-wheelers across the country, including in city corporations and urban areas. State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam chaired the meeting.
The information adviser said a large number of battery-powered rickshaws are already operating across the country and the issue cannot be addressed by simply denying their existence.
“This is a reality. We need to bring this reality into a policy,” he said.
He said the policy would determine whether the technical specifications of vehicles currently in operation meet safety standards, which types of vehicles would be approved, how drivers would be licensed, how vehicles would be registered and which categories of roads they would be allowed to use.
“If an effective policy is introduced, the chaos and uncertainty surrounding battery-powered rickshaws on the roads will be greatly reduced,” Zahed Ur Rahman said.

item.title: Tarique pays tribute to Zia, Khaleda on BNP’s founding anniversary
item.description:
BNP Chairman and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Tuesday paid homage to slain party founder Ziaur Rahman and its former chairperson Khaleda Zia by placing a wreath at their graves, marking the party’s 48th founding anniversary.
Tarique, also the eldest son of Zia and Khaleda, flanked by party senior leaders, placed the wreath at his parents’ graves at She r-e-Bangla Nagar around 9:20am and offered fateha there.
They also offered Fateha and joined a munajat seeking eternal peace for the departed souls of the party’s founder and former chairperson.
BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, Standing Committee members Gayeshwar Chandra Roy, Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan, Salahuddin Ahmed, Selima Rahman, Dr AZM Zahid Hossain, Aman Ullah Aman, Farhad Halim Donar and Ismail Zabihullah, Vice Chairman Nurul Islam Moni, Joint Secretaries General Khairul Kabir Khokon, Habib-un-Nabi Khan Sohel, Shahid Uddin Chowdhury Anee and Syed Emran Saleh Prince, Abdus Salam Azad, Treasurer Rashiduzzaman Millat, Publicity Secretary Sultan Salahuddin Tuku and Dhaka North city unit president Aminul Haque, among others, present.
After Tarique left the grave premises and security restrictions were eased, a large number of BNP leaders, activists and supporters gathered there.
They chanted slogans such as “Shubho, Shubho, Shubho Din, BNP-r Jonmodin” and “Ek Zia Lokantore, Lokkho Zia Ghore Ghore”.
Leaders and activists of different BNP-affiliated organisations including that of Dhaka city units, Jubo Dal, Swechchhasebak Dal, Muktijoddha Dal, Krishak Dal, Mohila Dal, Tanti Dal, Matsyajibi Dal, Doctors Association of Bangladesh (DAB), Agriculturalists Association of Bangladesh (AAB), Jatiyatabadi Samajik Sangskritik Sangstha (Jasas) and Chhatra Dal, also paid homage at Ziaur Rahman’s grave.
The day’s programs began early in the morning with the national and party flags being hoisted at BNP’s central office in Nayapaltan and the chairman’s Gulshan office.
The BNP is observing a five-day central program to mark its founding anniversary. The programs include a central discussion at the capital on September 5, besides tree plantation and fish-release programs across the country.
The party and its associate organisations have published posters marking the anniversary, while various newspapers published special supplements.
Tarique Rahman and BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi issued separate messages congratulating party leaders, activists, supporters and well-wishers on the occasion.
Ziaur Rahman founded BNP on September 1, 1978, with a 19-point programme aimed at building a self-reliant Bangladesh. He led the party as its chairman, followed by Khaleda Zia and subsequently Tarique Rahman.
The BNP is celebrating its 48th founding anniversary at a significant juncture, having returned to state power after around two decades under Tarique Rahman’s leadership, with him serving as prime minister for the first time.
It is also the first founding anniversary the party is observing without Khaleda Zia, who died on December 30, 2025.

item.title: Rana Plaza corruption case: Verdict deferred as court schedules arguments
item.description:
A Dhaka court has moved the corruption case against eight people, including Rana Plaza owner Sohel Rana, from the verdict stage to the arguments stage to clarify certain issues before delivering its judgment.
Dhaka Divisional Special Judge BM Tariqul Kabir passed the order on his own motion on Tuesday without delivering the scheduled verdict.
ACC Prosecutor Istiaq Ahmed confirmed the matter, saying the judge had deferred the verdict to allow arguments on some issues. The court will deliver its judgment after hearing the arguments, he said.
The case was previously scheduled for verdict on August 16. However, the announcement was deferred to September 1 as the verdict was not ready.
Sohel Rana is out on bail in the corruption case but remains in jail in connection with the murder case filed over the Rana Plaza collapse. He was produced before the court from jail on Sunday.
Among the other accused, Mahbubur Rahman and Farzana Islam have been absconding since the case was filed. The other accused are out on bail and appeared before the court on Sunday.
During the trial, Sohel Rana’s father Abdul Khalek and mother Morjina Khatun Begum died. They were subsequently acquitted in the case.
On April 24, 2013, the 10-storey Rana Plaza building near Savar bus stand collapsed, trapping around 5,000 workers from several garment factories operating inside the building.
Rescuers recovered 1,136 bodies and rescued 2,438 people alive from the rubble. Around 2,000 of those rescued were injured or left disabled.
Five days after the disaster, RAB arrested Sohel Rana in Benapole, Jessore, on April 29 as he was allegedly attempting to flee to India.
The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) began investigating allegations of corruption in the construction of the building soon after the collapse.
On June 15, 2014, ACC Deputy Assistant Director SM Mofidul Islam filed a case against 17 people with Savar police station for allegedly constructing the building in violation of the approved design.
The building was registered in the name of Sohel Rana’s father, and the initial case excluded his parents. However, the subsequent investigation found that Sohel Rana was the main person responsible for the building, leading to his inclusion in the charge sheet.
On February 23, 2017, the investigation officer submitted a further investigation report accusing 18 people. The court later acquitted eight of them and ordered charges to be framed against the remaining 10.
According to the further investigation report, Savar Municipality approved a design on April 10, 2006, for a six-storey shopping complex named Rana Plaza.
On January 22, 2008, approval was sought to add four more floors to the six-storey structure. The municipal authorities subsequently opened new files, concealing information from the earlier approval documents, and approved the design for a 10-storey building.
Although the original plan was for a shopping complex, the Savar Municipality later allowed five garment factories to operate in the building.
After the charge sheet was filed against the accused on May 21, 2017, the trial began. During the trial, 19 of the 20 prosecution witnesses testified before the court.
Two other cases are pending against Sohel Rana — one for murder in connection with the Rana Plaza collapse and another for violating building construction regulations.

item.title: Sundarbans reopens after three-month fishing, tourism ban
item.description:
The Sundarbans reopened to tourists and forest-dependent people on Tuesday after a three-month ban aimed at protecting fish breeding and preserving the biodiversity of the world’s largest mangrove forest.
Fishermen and other forest-dependent people from villages and upazilas adjacent to the Sundarbans have completed preparations to return to the forest with valid passes and permits to catch fish and crabs.
The reopening has brought relief to thousands of families who depend directly or indirectly on the forest for their livelihoods after remaining without work for three months.
However, security concerns remain among them, particularly regarding extortion, harassment and possible abductions by forest criminals.
Forest-dependent people said the number of people relying on the Sundarbans for their livelihoods is much higher than the number officially registered with the government.
Preparations have created a buzz at river ghats and fishing villages adjacent to the Sundarbans.
Fishermen are repairing torn nets, applying tar to old boats and checking the engines of their trawlers. They are also preparing equipment needed for crab collection.
Many families remained without work during the three-month ban and are now facing pressure to repay loans.
The annual fishing ban is imposed during the monsoon breeding season to allow fish to reproduce and protect the forest’s biodiversity.
During this year’s three-month closure, Sundarbans-dependent families had to rely on alternative sources of income to make ends meet.
Meanwhile, preparations have also been completed for tourist vessels, including ships and launches, to resume operations as the Sundarbans is one of the country’s major tourist destinations.
Khulna Divisional Forest Officer (DFO) Hasanur Rahman said the three-month closure contributed positively to the forest ecosystem.
“With public access to the forest suspended for three months, vegetation has grown considerably, while the number of deer and other species of wildlife and birds has increased,” he said.
He added that fish production in the rivers and canals flowing through the Sundarbans has also increased during the closure.
The reopening is expected to restore economic activity among communities dependent on fishing, crab collection, tourism and other forest-related activities, while authorities will continue to regulate access through the pass-and-permit system.
According to forest department data, the total revenue generated from the Sundarbans stood at Tk 6,75,81,291 in the 2025-26 fiscal year, compared to Tk7,57,17,994.97 in the 2024-25 fiscal year.

item.title: Dhaka ranks 11th among cities with worst air quality
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 11th among the world’s cities with the worst air quality on Tuesday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 105 at 10:08am.
According to the AQI scale, the city's air quality was classified as “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups”, posing health risks to children, older adults, and people with heart or lung diseases, while the general public is mostly unaffected.
Kuching in Malaysia topped the global pollution list with an AQI of 579, followed by Dubai in the United Arab Emirates with 184 and Kinshasa in the Democratic Republic of Congo with 167.
An AQI reading of 101 to 150 is considered ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’, while 151 to 200 is classified as ‘unhealthy’. A reading between 201 and 300 is considered ‘very unhealthy’, and anything above 301 is categorized as ‘hazardous’, posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides a daily indication of air quality by measuring the level of pollution and its potential impact on human health.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants — particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long faced serious air pollution problems, with air quality generally deteriorating during the winter months and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution contributes to around 7 million deaths worldwide every year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Gas crisis hits consumers hard in Savar
item.description:
The gas crisis in Savar has persisted for nearly one and a half months, leaving residential consumers without cooking gas, CNG drivers waiting for hours at filling stations and industries struggling to keep their operations running.
Residents said they often get little to no gas throughout the day and night, forcing them to rely on LPG cylinders, electric stoves and firewood for cooking.
During a visit to several homes on College Road in Savar municipality, residents described the situation as increasingly difficult.
“There has been no gas for two months. We have to buy firewood, and now even firewood is becoming scarce,” said Naznin Sultana, a tenant in the Radio Colony area.
Another resident, Tania Akter, said: “We cannot afford to buy a cylinder, yet we have to pay the monthly gas bill. We are suffering a lot. Because of the gas shortage, sometimes we can manage only one meal a day.”
The crisis is also affecting CNG filling stations in Savar.
Of seven stations in Aminbazar, Hemayetpur and Savar municipality, five are reportedly experiencing low gas pressure, resulting in long queues of vehicles.
CNG driver Nur Alam said he had been waiting for hours without getting gas.
“I arrived at around 8am, and it is now 1pm. I still haven’t got gas,” he said.
Bus driver Shahidul Islam, who came to Savar from Manikganj, said the shortage was affecting drivers travelling across the area.
“We cannot find gas anywhere. The situation is the same day and night. We are suffering tremendously,” he said.
Business owners and industrial operators said gas pressure, which normally remains between 8 and 10 PSI, has fallen to around 2-3 PSI.
“A CNG station normally needs 8 to 10 PSI to operate, but we are getting only around 3 PSI,” said Humayun Kabir, an official at a CNG station in Savar.
The shortage has also disrupted industrial production, with factories being forced to rely on generators.
Khairul Alam, an official at a garment factory in Hemayetpur, said the factory was having to arrange fuel regularly to keep its generators running.
“Industries around us are also running their generators at the same time, making the fuel shortage increasingly severe,” he said.
When contacted, Abu Saleh Mohammad Khademuddin, manager of the Savar zonal office of Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Limited, declined to comment on the situation.

item.title: Eight injured as bus overturns on Padma Bridge
item.description:
Eight people were seriously injured after a Dhaka-bound passenger bus lost control and overturned on the Mawa-end slope of the Padma Bridge in Munshiganj on Monday afternoon.
The accident disrupted traffic on the Dhaka-bound lane for nearly 45 minutes before the overturned bus was removed and the road was cleared.
Muhammad Shofiqul Islam, deputy assistant director of Munshiganj Fire Service and Civil Defence, said the “New Green Line Express” bus was travelling to Dhaka from Magura when the accident occurred.
He said the bus lost control due to excessive speed while descending the bridge, hit the roadside railing and overturned.
Two rescue teams from Sreenagar Fire Station soon arrived and rescued the injured passengers from the bus.
The injured were taken to Sreenagar Upazila Health Complex in fire service ambulances.
The injured were identified as Saifullah, 80; Md Lutfar, 63; Rebeka Khatun, 40; Nur Islam, 46; Rashida, 40; Fatema, 7; Saif, 23; and Arafat, 13.

item.title: Civil aviation minister: Bangladesh buying 14 Boeing aircraft, plans to lease more
item.description:
Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat on Monday said Bangladesh is buying 14 Boeing aircraft from the United States and it has also plans to lease some additional aircraft.
“The US had requested that Bangladesh use Boeing aircraft, and the government is acting accordingly,” he told reporters, responding to a question over the government’s reported plan to purchase Boeing aircraft from the United States.
The minister attended a law-and-order and development coordination meeting as the chief guest at the conference room of the Mymensingh deputy commissioner in the afternoon.
Millat said Bangladesh will procure new aircraft from Airbus, jointly manufactured by France, Britain and Germany, as part of efforts to modernise and strengthen the aviation sector.
U.S. Special Envoy for South and Central Asia and its Ambassador to India Sergio Gor has said Bangladesh has committed billions of dollars to buy additional Boeing aircraft from the United States under a new deal between Dhaka and Washington.
In April, Bangladesh signed a deal with US aircraft manufacturer Boeing to buy 14 planes for its national carrier Biman Bangladesh Airlines, the two sides announced - the airline’s biggest-ever order, in a deal valued at $3.7 billion.
The government is working round the clock to resolve the existing problems in the country’s power and energy sectors, describing the current electricity and gas crisis as a “mess” left by its predecessors.
He said a sustainable solution to the crisis would take time and strict action would be taken against those seeking to create disorder and administrative instability.
“Gas and electricity during Sheikh Hasina’s time have left us in trouble. But we are carrying this trouble; we did not create it,” he said.
Responding to criticism over the electricity and gas shortages, the minister said some opposition lawmakers and representatives of Jamaat-e-Islami frequently stage movements demanding the government step down for failing to ensure adequate power and gas supplies.
“But if you ask us to step down, can you provide electricity tomorrow? Can you provide electricity or gas within six months? You cannot,” he said.
Millat said resolving the crisis and developing new infrastructure would require time.
“Even after laying the foundation stone of a building, it takes at least two years to complete it. Even if we work rapidly using new technologies, it will still take one-and-a-half to two years,” he said.
“We are working day and night toward that goal,” he added.
The minister also urged law-enforcement agencies and administration officials to take strict measures against those attempting to create social and administrative instability.
“We must not create disorder at every turn. Those who want to create social and administrative instability must be dealt with firmly,” he said, instructing officials to properly enforce existing laws.
“Our only goal is to ensure that people live in peace and get a better Bangladesh,” he said.
Senior officials of the local administration, lawmakers, representatives of law-enforcement agencies and officials from different government departments were also present.

item.title: Three arrested over Tk 38L robbery in Dhanmondi

DMP Deputy Commissioner (Media and Public Relations) Aktar Hossain confirmed the arrests.
The robbery took place around noon on Sunday near Dhanmondi Lake when a man carrying the money after withdrawing it from a bank in Dhanmondi was intercepted by three men riding a motorcycle.
The robbers snatched his bag containing the money and fled, police said.
The victim immediately chased them. At one point, one of the suspects fell off the motorcycle and was caught by local residents, who also recovered a revolver and four rounds of ammunition from him.
After being informed, police from Dhanmondi Model Police Station went to the scene and arrested the suspect, identified as Tanvir Abedin, 41.
Later, Dhanmondi police and the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Detective Branch (DB) conducted a joint operation with Tanvir and arrested two other alleged members of the robbery gang—Md Mojibur Rahman, 60, and Md Zakir Hossain, alias Captain Zakir, 60.

item.title: Rangpur murders: Dope tests of two accused negative
item.description:
The dope test reports of two accused in the Rangpur four-murder case have come back negative, with no evidence of drug use found in their blood or urine samples.
Rangpur Metropolitan Detective Branch (DB) Deputy Commissioner Sanatan Chakraborty confirmed the matter on Monday afternoon, saying no signs of drug use were detected.
The samples of accused Mugdha Das and Siddharth Das, who are currently in Rangpur Central Jail, were collected on Sunday after the court approved a request for their dope tests.
Investigating DB police Officer-in-Charge Jinnat Ali said the accused were not taken out of the prison for security reasons. Instead, technologists from Rangpur Medical College were brought to the jail to collect their blood and urine samples.
Rangpur Medical College technologist Mohammad Ashraf said urine samples were collected from the two accused for testing.
Sanatan Chakraborty, also the spokesperson for Rangpur Metropolitan Police, said the case was highly sensitive and there was a risk of attacks or mob gatherings if the accused were taken outside the prison.
He said the tests conducted at the Rangpur Medical College laboratory found no evidence of drug use and the reports were subsequently submitted as negative.
Sanatan Chakraborty declined to comment further on the reports.
The negative dope tests have raised questions about the police’s earlier account of the motive behind the killings.
Police had said the accused, Siddharth and Mugdha Das, consumed four yaba tablets at their friend Simanta Das’s house before going to the home of retired schoolteacher Ganapati Chakraborty.
According to the police account, they later went to the house of alleged drug dealer Shanto and bought four more yaba tablets by pawning their mobile phones. They then climbed onto the roof of a neighbouring house and entered Ganapati’s roof, where they allegedly consumed yaba.
Police said Ganapati saw them, shouted and threatened them, after which the accused allegedly killed him and three members of his family.
The police’s account has come under renewed scrutiny following the negative dope test results.
On the night of August 22, police recovered the bodies of Ganapati Chakraborty, his wife, daughter and son from a locked house in the Masuapara, also known as Daspara, area of Rangpur city.
Neighbours Mugdha Das and Siddharth Das were subsequently arrested in connection with the killings.
Ganapati’s elder brother Gopinath Chakraborty filed a murder case with Kotwali police station.
The two accused later gave confessional statements under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before a court.
The case is currently being investigated by the police’s Detective Branch.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 973 as six die in 24 hours
item.description:
Six more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Monday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 973.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all six of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 874, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 99, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the six new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with five deaths reported in the Dhaka division and four in Dhaka district.
A total of 1,162 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Monday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 157,991.
During the same period, 94 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 19,312.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 138,445 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 133,404 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: High Court upholds death sentence in Magura child rape-murder case
item.description:
The High Court has upheld the death sentence of Hitu Sheikh in the widely discussed rape and murder case of an eight-year-old child in Magura.
A High Court bench comprising Justice Bhishmadev Chakraborty and Justice KM Rasheduzzaman Raja began announcing the verdict at 11am on Monday.
The verdict was initially scheduled for August 25 but was deferred after the state sought more time.
State-appointed lawyer Hafizur Rahman Khan represented Hitu Sheikh, while Deputy Attorney General Imam Hasan Tarek appeared for the state, assisted by Assistant Attorney General Rohani Siddique and Mahbuba Tasnim Ankhi.
The hearing on the death reference and appeal began on August 11.
In early March 2025, the child was allegedly raped and sexually assaulted while visiting her sister's in-laws in Nijnanduali village of Magura. She was initially taken to hospitals in Magura and Faridpur in critical condition. As her condition deteriorated, she was transferred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital and later to Combined Military Hospital, where she died on March 13.
On May 17, 2025, Magura Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal Judge M Zahid Hasan sentenced the main accused, the father-in-law of the child's sister, to death. The court acquitted the other three accused.
The case documents were subsequently sent to the High Court as a death reference.
Amid several incidents of violence against women and children, Chief Justice Zubair Rahman Chowdhury formed a special High Court bench on June 10, 2026, to prioritise death references and appeals in cases under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act.
A special team of state lawyers was also formed to assist the bench. Led by Attorney General Barrister Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal, the team includes deputy attorney generals Mohammad Imam Hossain Tarek and Syed Ejaz Kabir, and assistant attorney generals Mahbuba Tasnim Ankhi, Mustafizur Rahman Mukul, Ashraful Alam, Rohani Siddique and Al Amin Siddique.

item.title: Makkah Pact: FM says no reason for anyone to be upset or worried
item.description:
Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman on Sunday reiterated that the "Makkah Pact" is an internal matter of the world Muslim family and that there is no reason for anyone to be upset or worried about this.
“This is not a matter of threatening. This is not a matter of attacking anyone. This is a matter of self-defense of our world Muslim family. So I do not see any reason for anyone to be upset or worried about this,” he said.
Dr Khalilur left Dhaka on Sunday night for New York to take up his responsibilities as president of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly, a tenure that will coincide with a crucial period for the world body, including the selection of a new UN secretary-general.
The foreign minister left Dhaka shortly after 8:20pm on an official visit to New York, US, in connection with his UNGA presidency from August 31 to October 21 and is scheduled to transit through Dubai, a senior official told UNB.
Asked about possible challenges in discharging the two responsibilities, Dr Khalilur said diplomats deal with realities rather than hypothetical situations.
“Look, we are diplomats. We do not work on ‘ifs’. We work on reality,” he told private television channel "Independent TV" in an interview before leaving Dhaka for New York.
The 81st session of the General Assembly will formally open on September 8, with world leaders expected to gather at UN Headquarters in New York later in the month for the annual high-level general debate.
The foreign minister said Bangladesh will maintain good relations with all countries while firmly protecting its national interests, reiterating that the government’s foreign policy is guided by the principle of “Bangladesh First.”
“Bangladesh First” means that Bangladesh is not alone. It means that we will maintain our relations by ensuring our mutual interests,” he said.
Dr Khalilur, who is set to serve as president of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, said he does not anticipate any major difficulty in handling the two responsibilities simultaneously.
He said another state minister has been appointed to the Foreign Ministry and that he has worked closely with the minister.
“So I do not see any particular challenge in performing my duties,” he said.
Dr Khalilur said the Rohingya crisis and the broader issue of refugees and displaced people would be among his priorities as President of the UN General Assembly.
“Refugees, displaced people, these are part of my priorities. I said that during my election. So I will definitely have a strong eye on this,” he said.
The issue would receive special attention during the UN General Assembly’s High-Level Week beginning September 22.
“There will be a high-level side event and I will present my statement there as President of the General Assembly,” he said.
Dr Khalilur reiterated Bangladesh’s longstanding position that repatriation is the only sustainable solution to the Rohingya crisis.
“There is only one solution to this problem - repatriation,” he said.
Dr Khalilur noted that the position has now gained broad international recognition and that even the Myanmar government has acknowledged the issue, although Bangladesh disagrees with some of the figures provided by Myanmar.
“Not everything in diplomacy is done publicly. Most of it is done behind the scenes. And when there is a success or failure, you see it face to face,” he said.
Assuming the presidency at a time of deepening geopolitical divisions, the Foreign Minister has pledged to make consensus-building and restoring confidence in the UN central to his tenure.
“The UN will commence its ninth decade at a time when trust in our organization is being tested on multiple fronts,” Dr Khalilur told UN member states.
He said the challenges facing the international community were undermining public trust and confidence in the UN’s ability to deliver on its commitments.
“As your president, I will dedicate myself to rebuilding trust, nurturing consensus, and opening space for good-faith negotiations that will lead to outcomes for all that are owned by all,” he said.
Dr Khalilur has also pledged to serve as a bridge-builder among member states, engage all sides, and work to find common ground amid widening divisions.
He said he would uphold the UN Charter and ensure geographical and gender balance within the Office of the President of the General Assembly while remaining attentive to the needs of smaller delegations.
Bangladesh is also expected to use the high-profile presidency to advance issues of national and regional importance, particularly the protracted Rohingya crisis.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam recently said Dhaka hopes to use its stronger diplomatic position at the UN to intensify international pressure on Myanmar and build momentum for a political and durable solution to the crisis.
“We are trying to involve the international community more,” she said, referring to a high-level UN session on the Rohingya crisis expected to be held in September, with Bangladesh’s Prime Minister Tarique Rahman expected to participate.
Shama Obaed said Dhaka hopes the high-level discussion will produce clearer international guidelines and stronger momentum towards resolving the crisis, which has become increasingly complex amid security and other challenges.
Bangladesh has repeatedly called for sustained international engagement to ensure the safe, voluntary, and dignified return of the Rohingya to Myanmar, while seeking greater global support for addressing the humanitarian and security dimensions of the crisis.

'Friendship' founder Runa Khan wins Ramon Magsaysay Award
item.description:
Runa Khan, founder of Friendship, has been named a recipient of the 2026 Ramon Magsaysay Award for her more than two decades of leadership in developing locally led solutions that empower marginalised communities to live with greater opportunity, dignity and hope.
The Ramon Magsaysay Award is Asia’s premier prize and highest honour—widely regarded as “Asia's Nobel Prize”, recognising “greatness of spirit” and “transformative leadership in Asia”.
Runa Khan is the 14th recipient of the Award from Bangladesh, after, in particular, Muhammad Yunus, founder of Grameen and Mother Teresa from India, both of whom also received the Nobel Prize for Peace. Incidentally, Mother Teresa had travelled to Bangladesh in the nineties and blessed the river barge that would later become Friendship’s first hospital ship. Other outstanding awardees have also been the Fazle Hasan Abed, founder of Brac, the Dalai Lama and Japanese filmmaker Akira Kurasawa. The formal award ceremony will be held on 15 November in Manila, Philippines. On receiving the award, Runa Khan said: “It is with great happiness and profound humility that I accept the Ramon Magsaysay Award. There is no leader who walks alone, so it is an honour for me to receive this on behalf of the unaddressed communities, who allow us to walk beside them; and on behalf of my Friendship family whose tireless devotion makes this work possible every day. I thank also those who have trusted and walked this almost impossible path with me for 25 long years—just believing. My children whose patience and understanding awes me. This recognition is a wonderful responsibility, and I offer my deepest gratitude to the Ramon Magsaysay Award Foundation for their trust and for honouring the enduring faith and power of humanity.” For Runa Khan, the recognition honours a body of work that began in Bangladesh’s remote riverine communities and grew into an integrated model for delivering solutions based on a deep understanding and respect of local communities and their realities. What began with a single floating hospital has grown into a social purpose organisation serving 7.5 million people annually across healthcare, education, climate action, sustainable economic development, inclusive citizenship and cultural preservation. Its holistic approach reflects the interconnected challenges faced by remote communities. Under strong leadership, Friendship’s approach is simple: systems should be designed around people’s realities rather than expecting people to fit systems that cannot reach them. It recruits and trains local people and works with communities to shape the solutions meant for them, taking an inclusive approach by involving women and people with disabilities and connecting health, education, livelihoods, rights and climate resilience. Five years after founding Friendship in Bangladesh, Runa Khan took the initiative to establish Friendship in Luxembourg in 2006, Netherlands in 2007, the UK in 2010, France in 2015, and Belgium in 2018. Her vision was to work as closely as possible with donors and creating partners, thereby bypassing the long chains of intermediaries in international aid while preserving local ownership. That vision has proven to be extremely effective thanks to a strong community of supporters, both public and private. The International entities have stood by the side of Friendship Bangladesh at every stage of its development over the past 24 years.
In her official Ramon Magsaysay Award citation, Runa Khan is being recognised for “her profound empathy for the poorest of the poor in her country, and her courage, vision, and tenacity in building and leading Friendship to accomplish her mission. In her hands, privilege became not an entitlement, but a responsibility; not a family legacy to protect, but a gift to be shared so that others, too, might have the chance to live with hope, opportunity, and dignity.” The Ramon Magsaysay Award was first given in 1958 in memory of the seventh Philippine President Ramon Magsaysay.
In 68 years, the Award has been bestowed on 328 individuals and 28 organisations whose selfless service has offered their societies in 24 countries across Asia, and the rest of the world solutions to some of the most challenging problems of human development.

item.title: Nepal buries dead as rescuers seek thousands missing
item.description:
Nepal was burying on Monday some of the hundreds of bodies retrieved after a deadly, tsunami-like flood crashed through the Himalayan region, sweeping away villages and leaving thousands still missing.
Distraught families have packed rescue stations and hospitals in search of their missing relatives, while others have faced the grim task of identifying bodies at overflowing morgues.
The huge wave of ice, rocks and debris that smashed into villages and towns on Wednesday claimed at least 797 lives in both Nepal and Tibet -- across the border in China -- with reports of some bodies possibly swept downstream as far as India.
At least 3,048 people remain missing, including many tourists and pilgrims to Tibet's sacred Mount Kailash. There are also 933 workers at hydropower plants among those unaccounted for in Nepal.
Nepali army troops and engineers drilled through debris on Sunday towards workers believed trapped in a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydroelectric site in the Himalayan river valley after they successfully inserted a pipe into the passage.
Workers who managed to get out described horrifying scenes when the disaster struck.
Surendra Dowluri, 33, from India's Andhra Pradesh state, said raging water swamped the Upper Trishuli-1 site, where he was working.
"We heard a very loud sound... and saw that the turbine floor was submerged with slush, and six workers were stuck in that," Dowluri told AFP in the Nepali capital Kathmandu after his rescue four days into the disaster.
"We managed to rescue five of them, but one person lost his life," he said, describing how some workers reached higher ground or construction areas out of reach of the torrent.
Overnight rain and rising river waters also hampered rescue operations on Sunday, filling the excavation area with water before conditions eased, the Nepali army said.
The disaster was caused by a glacial collapse, sending a wall of water and debris downstream, the US Geological Survey said.
The torrent caused the formation of huge lakes, closely watched by emergency workers for risks to their operations.
Chinese rescuers near the Tibet border port that was hit by a deadly mudslide were "moved to a safe location" on Sunday after a new lake was formed by a landslide, state media reported.
China has so far put the death toll in Tibet at 16, with the number of missing at 546.
In Nepal, the disaster agency raised the total number of people missing on its side of the border to 2,502 on Sunday, saying there were also 781 confirmed deaths.
Overwhelmed by the number of bodies and without proper freezing facilities, Nepali authorities have had to begin burials before completing the identification process.
Officials said DNA samples were taken from the bodies so that families could later claim them and perform traditional funeral rites.
Grieving relatives gathered at identification centres to watch LED screens showing pictures of retrieved bodies, occasionally closing their eyes when the grim exercise overwhelmed them.
Walking out from one such building next to a makeshift morgue, Shobha Adhikary told a local coordinator she believed one image showed her childhood best friend.
"It looks like him, for sure," she said, showing coordinators a photograph of a smiling, middle-aged man.
"My husband and I are best friends with Rajkumar and his wife Geeta," she said. Geeta has also been missing since Wednesday.
Survivors were also faced with the daunting prospect of rebuilding their lives from nothing.
"All the settlements near the river were swept away," resident Buddhi Ram Dangol told AFP in Nepal's Nuwakot district.
"There is nothing left."
The United States and Canada said they would provide $3.6 million each in humanitarian aid to Nepal.
The UK has offered $6.8 million, while the UN released $2.5 million in emergency funding, and aid pledges were made by the European Union, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, and others.
Nepal's economy is already under pressure, with limited resources to respond to a disaster of this scale. Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said the reconstruction bill could run into "billions of dollars".
He appealed for specialised assistance, including heavy-lift drones and technology to help locate people who are trapped.
Khanal also called for forensic testing kits to identify corpses and freezer units to store them, saying bodies that have been in water could decompose at a faster rate.
The minister has highlighted the inequity that Nepal should suffer the extreme impacts of climate change when it has one of the world's lowest per-capita carbon emissions.
That is due to its location in the Himalayas, the world's highest mountain range, where glaciers are melting at rapid speed as the planet heats.
In Tibet, which is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists and where Chinese authorities are the only source of information, a total of 2,141 personnel have joined search and rescue operations.
In an illustration of the difficulties of access, Chinese rescuers seeking to establish a route to the Tibet epicentre of the disaster, Gyirong Port, only advanced 285 metres (935 feet) on Sunday.
They have another 1.25 kilometres to go before reaching the site, the state-run Xinhua news agency reported.
